Every operation below conforms to the [TaskFlow API Documentation Style Guide](taskflow_api_style_guide.md); parameters, enums, defaults, and status codes are reconciled against the OpenAPI 3.0 specification (v2.0.1) extracted from the codebase.\\n\\n## Endpoint index\\n\\n### Open endpoints\\n\\n* [Authenticate a user](#authenticate-a-user) : `POST /auth/login`\\n* [Refresh an access token](#refresh-an-access-token) : `POST /auth/refresh`\\n\\n### Endpoints that require authentication\\n\\n#### Task related\\n\\n* [List tasks](#list-tasks) : `GET /tasks`\\n* [Create a task](#create-a-task) : `POST /tasks`\\n* [Retrieve a task](#retrieve-a-task) : `GET /tasks/{taskId}`\\n* [Update a task](#update-a-task) : `PUT /tasks/{taskId}`\\n* [Delete a task](#delete-a-task) : `DELETE /tasks/{taskId}`\\n* [Assign a task](#assign-a-task) : `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign`\\n\\n#### Project related\\n\\n* [List projects](#list-projects) : `GET /projects`\\n* [Create a project](#create-a-project) : `POST /projects`\\n* [Retrieve a project](#retrieve-a-project) : `GET /projects/{projectId}`\\n* [Update a project](#update-a-project) : `PUT /projects/{projectId}`\\n* [Delete a project](#delete-a-project) : `DELETE /projects/{projectId}`\\n\\n#### User related\\n\\n* [Retrieve the current user](#retrieve-the-current-user) : `GET /users/me`\\n\\n#### Webhook related\\n\\n* [Create a webhook](#create-a-webhook) : `POST /webhooks`\\n* [Delete a webhook](#delete-a-webhook) : `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}`\\n\\n#### Search related\\n\\n* [Search tasks](#search-tasks) : `GET /search/tasks`\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Authentication\\n\\nTaskFlow v2 supports two credential types. Include either one in the `Authorization` header of every request to a protected endpoint:\\n\\n```plaintext\\nAuthorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\n```\\n\\n1. **Static API tokens.** Generate a long-lived API token from the TaskFlow dashboard under **Settings > API Keys**. Use these for server-to-server integrations that do not act on behalf of an individual user.\\n2. **Login token pairs.** Exchange a user's credentials for an access token and a refresh token with [`POST /auth/login`](#authenticate-a-user). Access tokens are short-lived; renew them with [`POST /auth/refresh`](#refresh-an-access-token). Use these for integrations that act on behalf of a user.\\n\\nIf credentials are missing, malformed, or expired, the API returns `401 Unauthorized` in the [standard error format](#errors).\\n\\n### Authenticate a user\\n\\nExchanges an email address and password for an access token and refresh token.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nPOST /api/v2/auth/login\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute    | Type   | Required | Description                                                                 |\\n|--------------|--------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `email`      | string | Yes      | The user's email address.                                                   |\\n| `password`   | string | Yes      | The user's password.                                                        |\\n| `mfa_code`   | string | Conditional | Time-based one-time code. Required if MFA is enabled on the account.     |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with a token pair:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"access_token\\\": \\\"at_9f2c...\\\",\\n  \\\"refresh_token\\\": \\\"rt_1a8e...\\\",\\n  \\\"token_type\\\": \\\"Bearer\\\",\\n  \\\"expires_in\\\": 3600\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning              | Common causes                                                        |\\n|-------------|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Invalid credentials  | Unknown email, wrong password.                                       |\\n| `403`       | MFA required         | MFA is enabled on the account and `mfa_code` was absent or invalid.  |\\n\\n### Refresh an access token\\n\\nExchanges a valid refresh token for a new token pair.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nPOST /api/v2/auth/refresh\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute       | Type   | Required | Description                          |\\n|-----------------|--------|----------|--------------------------------------|\\n| `refresh_token` | string | Yes      | The refresh token issued by login.   |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` and a new token pair (same shape as the login response).\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning                             | Common causes                                    |\\n|-------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Refresh token expired or revoked    | Token older than its validity window, or rotated/revoked by logout. |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Tasks\\n\\nUse this API to create, retrieve, update, and delete tasks, the primary work units in TaskFlow.\\n\\n### List tasks\\n\\nLists all tasks the authenticated user can access, with filtering, sorting, and pagination.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nGET /api/v2/tasks\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute    | Type    | Required | Description                                                                        |\\n|--------------|---------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `status`     | string  | No       | Filter by task status. One of `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived`, `blocked`.|\\n| `project_id` | integer | No       | Only return tasks belonging to this project.                                       |\\n| `page`       | integer | No       | Page number to return. Default is `1`.                                             |\\n| `per_page`   | integer | No       | Number of results per page. Default is `25`. Maximum is `200`.                     |\\n| `sort`       | string  | No       | Sort field. One of `created_at`, `updated_at`, `priority`, `due_date`.             |\\n| `order`      | string  | No       | Sort direction. One of `asc`, `desc`.                                              |\\n| `label`      | string  | No       | Filter tasks by label name.                                                        |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` and a paginated envelope with the following response attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute           | Type          | Description                              |\\n|---------------------|---------------|------------------------------------------|\\n| `data`              | object array  | The page of task objects.                |\\n| `data[].id`         | integer       | Task ID.                                 |\\n| `data[].title`      | string        | Task title.                              |\\n| `data[].status`     | string        | Task status.                             |\\n| `data[].priority`   | string        | Task priority.                           |\\n| `meta.current_page` | integer       | Page number returned.                    |\\n| `meta.total_pages`  | integer       | Total number of pages available.         |\\n| `meta.total_count`  | integer       | Total number of matching tasks.          |\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks?status=open&page=1\\\"\\n```\\n\\nExample response:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"data\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"id\\\": 1042,\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"Fix login bug\\\",\\n      \\\"description\\\": \\\"Users are unable to login with SSO\\\",\\n      \\\"status\\\": \\\"open\\\",\\n      \\\"priority\\\": \\\"high\\\",\\n      \\\"assignee_id\\\": 57,\\n      \\\"project_id\\\": 12,\\n      \\\"created_at\\\": \\\"2024-03-01T14:22:00Z\\\",\\n      \\\"updated_at\\\": \\\"2024-03-01T14:22:00Z\\\",\\n      \\\"due_date\\\": \\\"2024-03-15T00:00:00Z\\\"\\n    }\\n  ],\\n  \\\"meta\\\": {\\n    \\\"current_page\\\": 1,\\n    \\\"total_pages\\\": 5,\\n    \\\"total_count\\\": 98\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning              | Common causes                          |\\n|-------------|----------------------|----------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized         | Missing or invalid token.              |\\n| `429`       | Too Many Requests    | Rate limit exceeded. See [Rate limiting](#rate-limiting). |\\n\\n### Create a task\\n\\nCreates a task. Only `title` is required; all other attributes are optional.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nPOST /api/v2/tasks\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute      | Type          | Required | Description                                                                     |\\n|----------------|---------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `title`        | string        | Yes      | Title of the task. Maximum 200 characters.                                      |\\n| `description`  | string        | No       | Longer description. Supports Markdown formatting.                               |\\n| `status`       | string        | No       | Initial status. Default is `open`.                                              |\\n| `priority`     | string        | No       | One of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`, `urgent`.                           |\\n| `assignee_id`  | integer       | No       | ID of the user to assign the task to.                                           |\\n| `project_id`   | integer       | No       | Project to create the task in. If omitted, the task is placed in the user's default project *(behavior pending engineering verification)*. |\\n| `due_date`     | string        | No       | Due date. ISO 8601 date-time (`2024-04-01T00:00:00Z`).                          |\\n| `tags`         | string array  | No       | Tags to apply to the task.                                                      |\\n| `watchers`     | integer array | No       | User IDs to add as watchers.                                                    |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `201 Created` with the full task object.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request POST \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n  --data '{\\n    \\\"title\\\": \\\"Design new landing page\\\",\\n    \\\"description\\\": \\\"Create mockups for the Q2 marketing campaign\\\",\\n    \\\"priority\\\": \\\"high\\\",\\n    \\\"project_id\\\": 12,\\n    \\\"due_date\\\": \\\"2024-04-01T00:00:00Z\\\",\\n    \\\"tags\\\": [\\\"design\\\", \\\"marketing\\\"],\\n    \\\"watchers\\\": [57, 82]\\n  }' \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning            | Common causes                                             |\\n|-------------|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `400`       | Bad request        | Malformed JSON body.                                      |\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized       | Missing or invalid token.                                 |\\n| `422`       | Validation error   | `title` missing or longer than 200 characters; invalid enum value. |\\n\\n### Retrieve a task\\n\\nRetrieves a single task by its ID.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nGET /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute  | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                      |\\n|------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `taskId`   | integer | Yes      | ID of the task to retrieve.                                                                      |\\n| `include`  | string  | No       | Expand related resources in the response. One of `comments`, `history`, `attachments`.           |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with the full task object (same schema as the list endpoint), plus the requested related resources when `include` is supplied.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042?include=comments\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning       | Common causes                                        |\\n|-------------|---------------|------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized  | Missing or invalid token.                            |\\n| `404`       | Task not found| Task does not exist or you do not have access to it. |\\n\\n### Update a task\\n\\nUpdates a task. Partial updates are supported: send only the fields you want to change; omitted fields remain unchanged. `id` and `created_at` cannot be modified.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nPUT /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute      | Type          | Required | Description                                                        |\\n|----------------|---------------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `taskId`       | integer       | Yes      | ID of the task to update.                                          |\\n| `title`        | string        | No       | New title.                                                         |\\n| `description`  | string        | No       | New description.                                                   |\\n| `status`       | string        | No       | Must be a valid status string.                                     |\\n| `priority`     | string        | No       | One of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`, `urgent`.              |\\n| `assignee_id`  | integer       | No       | Assignee's user ID. Set to `null` to unassign.                     |\\n| `project_id`   | integer       | No       | Move the task to this project.                                     |\\n| `due_date`     | string        | No       | ISO 8601 date-time. Set to `null` to clear.                        |\\n| `tags`         | string array  | No       | Replace the task's tags.                                           |\\n| `watchers`     | integer array | No       | Replace the task's watcher user IDs.                               |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` and the updated task object.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request PUT \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n  --data '{\\\"status\\\": \\\"in_progress\\\", \\\"assignee_id\\\": 57}' \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042\\\"\\n```\\n\\nExample response:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"id\\\": 1042,\\n  \\\"title\\\": \\\"Fix login bug\\\",\\n  \\\"status\\\": \\\"in_progress\\\",\\n  \\\"priority\\\": \\\"high\\\",\\n  \\\"assignee_id\\\": 57,\\n  \\\"project_id\\\": 12,\\n  \\\"updated_at\\\": \\\"2024-03-02T10:15:00Z\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning      | Common causes                                                            |\\n|-------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid token.                                                |\\n| `404`       | Task not found | Task does not exist or you do not have access to it.                   |\\n| `409`       | Conflict     | Concurrent modification detected: the task changed since you last read it. Re-fetch the task, re-apply your change, and retry. |\\n\\n### Delete a task\\n\\nDeletes a task permanently. This action cannot be undone.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nDELETE /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute | Type    | Required | Description               |\\n|-----------|---------|----------|---------------------------|\\n| `taskId`  | integer | Yes      | ID of the task to delete. |\\n\\nPermissions: you must be an admin or owner on the project that contains the task. Regular members can delete only tasks they created.\\n\\nIf successful, returns `204 No Content`. The response body is empty.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request DELETE \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning         | Common causes                                   |\\n|-------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------|\\n| `403`       | Forbidden       | Insufficient permissions on the project.        |\\n| `404`       | Task not found  | Task does not exist or you do not have access.  |\\n\\n### Assign a task\\n\\nAssigns a task to an assignee. Use this operation instead of `PUT /tasks/{taskId}` when the only change is assignment, because it additionally triggers assignment notifications.\\n\\nReassignment behavior: assigning a task that already has an assignee replaces the existing assignee. The previous assignee loses assignment notifications; watchers are unaffected.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nPOST /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}/assign\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute     | Type    | Required | Description                                                      |\\n|---------------|---------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `taskId`      | integer | Yes      | ID of the task to assign.                                        |\\n| `assignee_id` | integer | Yes      | ID of the user to assign the task to.                            |\\n| `notify`      | boolean | No       | Whether to send a notification to the assignee. Default is `true`. |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with the assigned task object.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request POST \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n  --data '{\\\"assignee_id\\\": 93, \\\"notify\\\": true}' \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1050/assign\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning              | Common causes                                       |\\n|-------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized         | Missing or invalid token.                           |\\n| `404`       | Task or user not found | `taskId` or `assignee_id` does not exist, or you lack access. |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Projects\\n\\nUse this API to manage projects, the containers that organize tasks and members.\\n\\n### List projects\\n\\nLists all projects the authenticated user has access to. Projects are returned in alphabetical order by name *(ordering pending engineering verification)*.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nGET /api/v2/projects\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute  | Type    | Required | Description                                                            |\\n|------------|---------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `archived` | boolean | No       | If `true`, include archived projects. Default is `false`.              |\\n| `role`     | string  | No       | Filter by your role in the project. One of `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `viewer`. |\\n| `page`     | integer | No       | Page number to return.                                                 |\\n| `per_page` | integer | No       | Number of results per page.                                            |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with a `projects` array.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects?archived=false\\\"\\n```\\n\\nExample response:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"projects\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"id\\\": 12,\\n      \\\"name\\\": \\\"Website Redesign\\\",\\n      \\\"description\\\": \\\"Q2 2024 website overhaul\\\",\\n      \\\"owner_id\\\": 57,\\n      \\\"created\\\": 1709312400,\\n      \\\"member_count\\\": 8,\\n      \\\"task_count\\\": 45,\\n      \\\"archived\\\": false\\n    }\\n  ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\n> [!warning]\\n> The `created` field is a Unix timestamp, not ISO 8601. This is a known legacy deviation; the TaskFlow timestamp standard is ISO 8601 UTC (see [Timestamps](#timestamps-and-formats)) and this field is scheduled to migrate in a future release.\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning      | Common causes             |\\n|-------------|--------------|---------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid token. |\\n\\n### Create a project\\n\\nCreates a project. `name` is required and must be unique within your organization, with a maximum of 100 characters.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nPOST /api/v2/projects\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute      | Type   | Required | Description                                                                       |\\n|----------------|--------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `name`         | string | Yes      | Project name. Maximum 100 characters; unique within the organization.             |\\n| `description`  | string | No       | Optional project description.                                                     |\\n| `template_id`  | integer| No       | Create from an existing project template.                                         |\\n| `visibility`   | string | No       | One of `private`, `internal`, `public`. Default is `private`.                     |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `201 Created` with the new project object (same fields as the list endpoint; `member_count` is `1`, `task_count` is `0`, and `archived` is `false` for new projects).\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request POST \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n  --data '{\\\"name\\\": \\\"My New Project\\\", \\\"visibility\\\": \\\"internal\\\"}' \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning            | Common causes                                        |\\n|-------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `400`       | Bad request        | Malformed JSON body.                                 |\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized       | Missing or invalid token.                            |\\n| `422`       | Validation error   | `name` missing, longer than 100 characters, or not unique. |\\n\\n### Retrieve a project\\n\\nRetrieves a single project by its ID.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nGET /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute   | Type    | Required | Description                    |\\n|-------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------|\\n| `projectId` | integer | Yes      | ID of the project to retrieve. |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with the project object.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/12\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning          | Common causes                                      |\\n|-------------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized     | Missing or invalid token.                          |\\n| `404`       | Project not found| Project does not exist or you do not have access.  |\\n\\n### Update a project\\n\\nUpdates a project. Partial updates are supported: send only the fields you want to change.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nPUT /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute     | Type    | Required | Description                                        |\\n|---------------|---------|----------|----------------------------------------------------|\\n| `projectId`   | integer | Yes      | ID of the project to update.                       |\\n| `name`        | string  | No       | New project name.                                  |\\n| `description` | string  | No       | New project description.                           |\\n| `archived`    | boolean | No       | Set to `true` to archive the project.              |\\n| `visibility`  | string  | No       | One of `private`, `internal`, `public`.            |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` and the updated project object.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request PUT \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n  --data '{\\\"description\\\": \\\"Q2 2024 website overhaul - updated scope\\\"}' \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/12\\\"\\n```\\n\\nExample response:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"id\\\": 12,\\n  \\\"name\\\": \\\"Website Redesign\\\",\\n  \\\"description\\\": \\\"Q2 2024 website overhaul - updated scope\\\",\\n  \\\"owner_id\\\": 57,\\n  \\\"archived\\\": false\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning           | Common causes                                     |\\n|-------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized      | Missing or invalid token.                         |\\n| `404`       | Project not found | Project does not exist or you do not have access. |\\n\\n### Delete a project\\n\\nDeletes a project permanently. This action cannot be undone.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nDELETE /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute   | Type    | Required | Description                                                        |\\n|-------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `projectId` | integer | Yes      | ID of the project to delete.                                       |\\n| `cascade`   | boolean | No       | If `true`, deletes all tasks within the project. \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/12?cascade=false\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning           | Common causes                                     |\\n|-------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized      | Missing or invalid token.                         |\\n| `403`       | API to retrieve information about the authenticated user.\\n\\n### Retrieve the current user\\n\\nRetrieves the profile of the currently authenticated user.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nGET /api/v2/users/me\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute | Type   | Required | Description                                                        |\\n|-----------|--------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `fields`  | string | No       | Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response.         |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with the user object.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/users/me?fields=id,email,name,timezone\\\"\\n```\\n\\nExample response:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"user\\\": {\\n    \\\"id\\\": 57,\\n    \\\"email\\\": \\\"jane@example.com\\\",\\n    \\\"name\\\": \\\"Jane Smith\\\",\\n    \\\"role\\\": \\\"admin\\\",\\n    \\\"organization_id\\\": 5,\\n    \\\"timezone\\\": \\\"America/New_York\\\",\\n    \\\"created_at\\\": \\\"2023-01-15T09:00:00Z\\\",\\n    \\\"last_login\\\": 1709398800\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n> [!warning]\\n> `created_at` is ISO 8601 but `last_login` is a Unix timestamp. This legacy deviation will be addressed in API v3.\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning      | Common causes             |\\n|-------------|--------------|---------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid token. |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Webhooks\\n\\nUse this API to manage webhooks, which deliver real-time event notifications to your integration endpoints. The complete list of event types, trigger conditions, payload examples, and provenance is maintained in the [Webhook Event Catalog](webhook_event_catalog.html).\\n\\n### Create a webhook\\n\\nCreates a webhook that delivers the selected event types to your webhook URL.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nPOST /api/v2/webhooks\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute | Type          | Required | Description                                                                 |\\n|-----------|---------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `url`     | string (URI)  | Yes      | The webhook URL that receives event deliveries.                             |\\n| `events`  | string array  | Yes      | Event types to subscribe to. One or more of: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `task.assigned`, `task.commented`, `project.created`, `project.archived`, `project.deleted`, `member.added`, `member.removed`. |\\n| `secret`  | string        | No       | HMAC secret for payload verification.                                       |\\n| `active`  | boolean       | No       | Whether the webhook delivers events. Default is `true`.                     |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `201 Created` with the created webhook object.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request POST \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Content-Type: application/json\\\" \\\\\\n  --data '{\\n    \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://integrations.acme.corp/taskflow/events\\\",\\n    \\\"events\\\": [\\\"task.created\\\", \\\"task.updated\\\", \\\"task.assigned\\\"],\\n    \\\"secret\\\": \\\"<your_hmac_secret>\\\",\\n    \\\"active\\\": true\\n  }' \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/webhooks\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Delivery guarantees.** Failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times; if every attempt fails, the delivery is marked `failed` (evidence: production delivery log, March 2024 export \u2014 delivery `d-90008`, HTTP 502, `retry_attempts: 3`, `final_status: failed`). Verify payload authenticity by computing an HMAC with your `secret` over the raw request body.\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning          | Common causes                              |\\n|-------------|------------------|--------------------------------------------|\\n| `400`       | Bad request      | Malformed JSON body.                       |\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized     | Missing or invalid token.                  |\\n| `422`       | Validation error | `url` is not a valid URI, or `events` contains an unknown event type. |\\n\\n### Delete a webhook\\n\\nDeletes a webhook permanently. The webhook URL stops receiving deliveries immediately; this action cannot be undone.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nDELETE /api/v2/webhooks/{webhookId}\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute   | Type    | Required | Description                    |\\n|-------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------|\\n| `webhookId` | integer | Yes      | ID of the webhook to delete.   |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `204 No Content`. The response body is empty.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request DELETE \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/webhooks/301\\\"\\n```\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning           | Common causes                                     |\\n|-------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized      | Missing or invalid token.                         |\\n| `404`       | Webhook not found | Webhook does not exist or you do not own it.      |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Search\\n\\nUse this API to find tasks by text and attribute filters.\\n\\n### Search tasks\\n\\nSearches tasks with a full-text query, optionally scoped by project, status, and date range.\\n\\n```plaintext\\nGET /api/v2/search/tasks\\n```\\n\\nSupported attributes:\\n\\n| Attribute    | Type    | Required | Description                                     |\\n|--------------|---------|----------|-------------------------------------------------|\\n| `q`          | string  | Yes      | Full-text search query.                         |\\n| `project_id` | integer | No       | Restrict results to this project.               |\\n| `status`     | string  | No       | Restrict results to this task status.           |\\n| `date_from`  | string  | No       | Lower bound (inclusive) on task dates. `YYYY-MM-DD`. |\\n| `date_to`    | string  | No       | Upper bound (inclusive) on task dates. `YYYY-MM-DD`. |\\n\\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with matching task objects.\\n\\nExample request:\\n\\n```bash\\ncurl --request GET \\\\\\n  --header \\\"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\\\" \\\\\\n  --url \\\"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/search/tasks?q=landing%20page&project_id=12\\\"\\n```\\n\\n> [!note]\\n> Advanced query syntax (operators, field-scoped terms) is supported only partially and is not yet fully specified. Contact API support before relying on operator behavior.\\n\\n**Errors**\\n\\n| Status code | Meaning      | Common causes                                        |\\n|-------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `400`       | Bad request  | `q` missing or invalid filter combination.           |\\n| `401`       | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid token.                            |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Rate limiting\\n\\nThe API enforces rate limits to ensure fair usage:\\n\\n- **Free tier:** 100 requests per minute.\\n- **Paid plans:** 1000 requests per minute.\\n\\nWhen you exceed the limit, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Check the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` response header to see how many requests you have left, and back off before retrying.\\n\\n## Pagination\\n\\nList endpoints support pagination via `page` and `per_page` query parameters. The response `meta` object contains pagination info (`current_page`, `total_pages`, `total_count`). The projects endpoint also accepts `page` and `per_page` per the OpenAPI specification; the earlier statement that it does not paginate was an error and has been removed.\\n\\n## Errors\\n\\nThe API uses standard HTTP status codes. The canonical v2 error body is:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"error\\\": {\\n    \\\"code\\\": \\\"VALIDATION_ERROR\\\",\\n    \\\"message\\\": \\\"Title is required\\\",\\n    \\\"details\\\": []\\n  }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nSome older endpoints may still return the legacy format:\\n\\n```json\\n{\\n  \\\"error\\\": \\\"not_found\\\",\\n  \\\"message\\\": \\\"Task not found\\\"\\n}\\n```\\n\\nTreat the canonical envelope as the contract for new integrations. The legacy format is transitional and will be removed.\\n\\n## Timestamps and formats\\n\\n- All request and response timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with a trailing `Z` (for example, `2024-03-01T14:22:00Z`), except the known legacy Unix-timestamp fields: project `created` and user `last_login`. Enum values are lowercase snake_case.\\n\\n## Changelog summary (docs reconciliation)\\n\\nThis reference was reconciled against the OpenAPI v2.0.1 spec and the documentation audit tracker. Highlights of what changed versus the previous ad-hoc docs:\\n\\n- Added the missing auth flow (`POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`) with MFA handling.\\n- Corrected task `title` maximum length (255 \u2192 200), `per_page` defaults (20/100 \u2192 25/200), and the `status`/`priority`/`sort` enums (`blocked`, `urgent`, `due_date` added).\\n- Documented `label` filtering and the `include` expansion parameter on task retrieval.\\n- Documented `watchers`, `409 Conflict` on task update, and the assign operation with `notify`.\\n- Documented project pagination (previously wrongly denied), `template_id`, `visibility`, project update and delete operations, and the `cascade` delete behavior.\\n- Documented the `fields` parameter on `GET /users/me`.\\n- Added full webhook and search reference sections, retry guarantees, and HMAC verification guidance.\\n\\n*For questions or support, email api-support@taskflow.io.*\\n\"}", "type": "tool_call"}]

\n

TaskFlow API — Webhook Event Catalog

\n

API version 2.0.1  |  Catalog compiled 2026-10-19

\n

\n This catalog synthesizes two sources: the event types declared in the OpenAPI 3.0 specification\n (taskflow_openapi_v2_extract.yaml, POST /webhooks events enum) and the event types\n observed in the production webhook delivery log (webhook 301 →\n https://integrations.acme.corp/taskflow/events, export 2024-03-10, 12 deliveries).\n

\n
\n\n
\n\n

Reconciliation summary

\n\n \n \n \n \n \n \n

Event types declared in OpenAPI spec10Subscribable via POST /webhooks
Event types observed in production log12All 10 declared types were observed in production

\n\n
\n Gap for engineering: task.due_date_approaching and task.overdue are live in\n production but absent from the OpenAPI events enum. \n\n

Provenance legend

\n

\n Declared + observed Event is in the OpenAPI events enum and was seen in the production delivery log.
\n Observed only Event was seen in production but is not declared in the OpenAPI spec.\n

\n\n

Delivery guarantees

\n

\n Failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times; if every attempt fails, the delivery is marked\n failed. Evidence: delivery d-90008 (project.deleted) returned HTTP\n 502 with retry_attempts: 3 and final_status: \"failed\" in the March 2024 export.\n The exact backoff interval is not specified in either source and is pending engineering confirmation.\n

\n

\n Payload authenticity: supply a secret when creating a webhook and verify the HMAC signature computed\n over the raw request body on each delivery.\n

\n\n

Event catalog

\n\n

Task events

\n\n
\n

task.createdDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a new task is created in any project your webhook can access.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A POST /tasks request succeeds (201 Created), or a task is created through the TaskFlow UI or a project template.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.created\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-01T14:22:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"task_id\": 1042,\n    \"project_id\": 12,\n    \"actor_id\": 57\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90001 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

task.updatedDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when one or more fields of an existing task change.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A PUT /tasks/{taskId} request succeeds, or an equivalent change is made in the UI. The payload lists exactly which fields changed via changed_fields.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.updated\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-01T15:05:33Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"task_id\": 1042,\n    \"changed_fields\": [\"status\", \"assignee_id\"],\n    \"actor_id\": 57\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90002 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

task.assignedDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a task is assigned to an assignee, including reassignment to a different assignee.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign request succeeds, or assignee_id is set via task update. Fires on the new assignment regardless of the notify flag (which controls email notification only).
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.assigned\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-05T10:02:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"task_id\": 1050,\n    \"assignee_id\": 93,\n    \"actor_id\": 57\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90006 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

task.commentedDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a comment is added to a task.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A comment is successfully attached to a task (UI or API).
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.commented\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-02T09:17:44Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"task_id\": 1042,\n    \"comment_id\": 5567,\n    \"actor_id\": 82\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90003 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

task.deletedDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a task is permanently deleted. Delivered after the deletion, so the referenced task no longer exists.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A DELETE /tasks/{taskId} request succeeds (204), or the containing project is deleted with cascade=true.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.deleted\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-08T09:00:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"task_id\": 999,\n    \"project_id\": 3,\n    \"actor_id\": 57\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90010 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

task.due_date_approachingObserved only

\n
\n
Description
\n
Scheduled reminder that a task's due date is approaching. Not declared in the OpenAPI spec; not subscribable via POST /webhooks as specified.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
Daily scheduled check. Production evidence: fired at exactly 00:00:00Z with days_remaining: 9, indicating a nightly job that fires when the task is within a fixed window of its due date.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.due_date_approaching\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-06T00:00:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"task_id\": 1042,\n    \"due_date\": \"2024-03-15T00:00:00Z\",\n    \"days_remaining\": 9\n  }\n}
\n Delivery d-90007 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

task.overdueObserved only

\n
\n
Description
\n
Scheduled notification that a task is past its due date. Not declared in the OpenAPI spec; not subscribable via POST /webhooks as specified.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
Daily scheduled check after midnight UTC once the due date has passed. Production evidence: fired at 00:00:00Z with days_overdue: 1.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.overdue\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-16T00:00:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"task_id\": 1042,\n    \"due_date\": \"2024-03-15T00:00:00Z\",\n    \"days_overdue\": 1\n  }\n}
\n Delivery d-90011 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n

Project events

\n\n
\n

project.createdDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a new project is created.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A POST /projects request succeeds (201), optionally from a template_id.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"project.created\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-09T13:55:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"project_id\": 15,\n    \"actor_id\": 82\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90012 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

project.archivedDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a project is archived. Archived projects remain readable but leave active workflows.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A PUT /projects/{projectId} request sets archived to true.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"project.archived\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-03T11:30:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"project_id\": 8,\n    \"actor_id\": 57\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90004 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

project.deletedDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a project is permanently deleted. With the default cascade=true, every task in the project is also deleted (each generating its own task.deleted event).
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A DELETE /projects/{projectId} request succeeds (204).
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"project.deleted\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-07T08:20:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"project_id\": 3,\n    \"actor_id\": 57\n  }\n}
\n Delivery d-90008 — failed after 3 retries (HTTP 502, final_status: failed)
\n
\n
\n\n

Membership events

\n\n
\n

member.addedDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a user is added to a project with a role.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A membership is granted on a project (UI invite or API). The payload includes the granted role.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"member.added\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-04T16:45:12Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"project_id\": 12,\n    \"user_id\": 93,\n    \"role\": \"member\",\n    \"actor_id\": 57\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90005 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n
\n

member.removedDeclared + observed

\n
\n
Description
\n
Fires when a user's membership on a project is removed.
\n
Trigger condition
\n
A membership is revoked on a project (UI or API). Task assignments held by the removed member are not automatically reassigned.
\n
Example payload
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"member.removed\",\n  \"timestamp\": \"2024-03-07T14:10:00Z\",\n  \"webhook_id\": 301,\n  \"data\": {\n    \"project_id\": 12,\n    \"user_id\": 45,\n    \"actor_id\": 57\n  }\n}
\n Reconstructed from delivery d-90009 (HTTP 200)
\n
\n
\n\n

Observations from the delivery log

\n
    \n
  • 12 deliveries, 11 successful, 1 failed (project.deleted, HTTP 502, exhausted 3 retries).
    • \n
  • All payload excerpts carry actor_id — the user who caused the event — except the two scheduled events (task.due_date_approaching, task.overdue), which are system-generated and have no actor.
    • \n
  • Scheduled events fire at exactly 00:00:00Z, consistent with a nightly batch job.
    • \n
\n\n
\n TaskFlow Technical Writing · Sources: taskflow_openapi_v2_extract.yaml (declared events),\n webhook_delivery_log.json (observed events), doc_audit_tracker.csv (retry-policy gap).\n Payloads are reconstructed from production delivery excerpts; field order and envelope keys are illustrative.\n
\n\n
\n\n\n","filePath":"/work/output/webhook_event_catalog.html"}", "type": "tool_call"}]

# Tone and style
You should be concise, direct, and to the point. When you run a non-trivial bash command, you should explain what the command does and why you are running it, to make sure the user understands what you are doing (this is especially important when you are running a command that will make changes to the user's system).
Remember that your output will be displayed on a command line interface. Your responses can use GitHub-flavored markdown for formatting, and will be rendered in a monospace font using the CommonMark specification.

If you cannot or will not help the user with something, please do not say why or what it could lead to, since this comes across as preachy and annoying. Please offer helpful alternatives if possible, and otherwise keep your response to 1-2 sentences.
Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid using emojis in all communication unless asked.

IMPORTANT: Keep your responses short, since they will be displayed on a command line interface. You MUST answer concisely with fewer than 4 lines (not including tool use or code generation), unless user asks for detail. You MUST avoid text before/after your response, such as "The answer is <answer>.", "Here is the content of the file..." or "Based on the information provided, the answer is..." or "Here is what I will do next...". Here are some examples to demonstrate appropriate verbosity:
<example>

# Proactiveness
You are allowed to be proactive, but only when the user asks you to do something. You should strive to strike a balance between:
1. Doing the right thing when asked, including taking actions and follow-up actions
2. Not surprising the user with actions you take without asking
For example, if the user asks you how to approach something, you should do your best to answer their question first, and not immediately jump into taking actions.

# Following conventions
When making changes to files, first understand the file's code conventions. Mimic code style, use existing libraries and utilities, and follow existing patterns.

# Code style

1: # TaskFlow API Documentation
2: 
3: **Version**: 2.0
4: **Last Updated**: March 2024
5: 
6: Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.
7: 
8: ## Authentication
9: 
10: All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:
11: 
12: ```
13: Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
14: ```
15: 
16: You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## Tasks
21: 
22: ### GET /api/v2/tasks
23: 
24: Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.
25: 
26: **Query Parameters**
27: 
28: | Parameter | Type | Description |
29: |-----------|------|-------------|
30: | status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |
31: | project_id | integer | Only return tasks belonging to this project |
32: | page | integer | Page number for pagination (default: 1) |
33: | per_page | integer | Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 100) |
34: | sort | string | Sort field. One of `created_at`, `updated_at`, `priority` |
35: | order | string | Sort direction: `asc` or `desc` |
36: 
37: **Example Request**
38: 
39: ```bash
40: curl -X GET "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks?status=open&page=1" \
41:   -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
42: ```
43: 
44: **Response** (200 OK)
45: 
46: ```json
47: {
48:   "data": [
49:     {
50:       "id": 1042,
51:       "title": "Fix login bug",
52:       "description": "Users are unable to login with SSO",
53:       "status": "open",
54:       "priority": "high",
55:       "assignee_id": 57,
56:       "project_id": 12,
57:       "created_at": "2024-03-01T14:22:00Z",
58:       "updated_at": "2024-03-01T14:22:00Z",
59:       "due_date": "2024-03-15T00:00:00Z"
60:     }
61:   ],
62:   "meta": {
63:     "current_page": 1,
64:     "total_pages": 5,
65:     "total_count": 98
66:   }
67: }
68: ```
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ### POST /api/v2/tasks
73: 
74: Creates a new task. You must provide at least a title. The task will be created under the user's default project if `project_id` is not specified.
75: 
76: **Request Body Arguments**
77: 
78: - `title` (string, **required**) - The title of the task. Max 255 characters.
79: - `description` (string) - A longer description. Supports Markdown formatting.
80: - `status` (string) - Initial status. Defaults to `open`.
81: - `priority` (string) - One of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`. Default is `medium`.
82: - `assignee_id` (integer) - User ID to assign the task to.
83: - `project_id` (integer) - Project to create the task in.
84: - `due_date` (string) - Due date in ISO 8601 format.
85: - `tags` (array of strings) - Tags to apply to the task.
86: 
87: **Example**
88: 
89: ```python
90: import requests
91: 
92: resp = requests.post(
93:     "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks",
94:     headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"},
95:     json={
96:         "title": "Design new landing page",
97:         "description": "Create mockups for the Q2 marketing campaign",
98:         "priority": "high",
99:         "project_id": 12,
100:         "due_date": "2024-04-01T00:00:00Z",
101:         "tags": ["design", "marketing"]
102:     }
103: )
104: print(resp.json())
105: ```
106: 
107: Returns `201 Created` on success with the full task object in the response body.
108: 
109: **Errors**
110: 
111: | Status Code | Meaning |
112: |------------|---------|
113: | 400 | Bad request - missing required fields or invalid values |
114: | 401 | Authentication failed |
115: | 422 | Validation error (e.g. title too long) |
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ### GET /api/v2/tasks/{id}
120: 
121: Get a single task by its ID.
122: 
123: Pass the task ID as a path parameter. Returns the task object if found. Returns 404 if the task doesn't exist or you don't have access.
124: 
125: Response includes the full task object (same schema as list endpoint).
126: 
127: No additional arguments.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ### Updating a task - PUT /api/v2/tasks/{id}
132: 
133: We support partial updates - you only need to send the fields you want to change. Any fields not included in the request body will remain unchanged.
134: 
135: Note: the `id` and `created_at` fields cannot be modified.
136: 
137: **Fields you can update:**
138: 
139: - title
140: - description
141: - status (must be a valid status string)
142: - priority
143: - assignee_id (set to `null` to unassign)
144: - project_id
145: - due_date (ISO 8601 timestamp or null to clear)
146: - tags
147: 
148: **Sample curl command:**
149: 
150: ```bash
151: curl -X PUT "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042" \
152:   -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
153:   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
154:   -d '{"status": "in_progress", "assignee_id": 57}'
155: ```
156: 
157: The API returns `200 OK` and the updated task object on success.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ### DELETE /api/v2/tasks/{id}
162: 
163: Permanently deletes a task. This action cannot be undone.
164: 
165: The user must have admin or owner permissions on the project that the task belongs to. Regular members can only delete tasks they created.
166: 
167: **Returns:**
168: 
169: `204 No Content` on success. The response body is empty.
170: 
171: If the task is not found a `404` error is returned. Attempting to delete a task without sufficient permissions results in `403 Forbidden`.
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## Projects
176: 
177: ### List projects
178: 
179: ```
180: GET /api/v2/projects
181: ```
182: 
183: This route returns all projects the authenticated user has access to. Projects are returned in alphabetical order by name.
184: 
185: **Query args:**
186: 
187: - `archived` (boolean) - if `true`, include archived projects. Default `false`.
188: - `role` (string) - filter by the user's role in the project: `owner`, `admin`, `member`
189: 
190: No authentication header examples are given here since it follows the same pattern described at the top of this doc.
191: 
192: **Sample response:**
193: 
194: ```json
195: {
196:   "projects": [
197:     {
198:       "id": 12,
199:       "name": "Website Redesign",
200:       "description": "Q2 2024 website overhaul",
201:       "owner_id": 57,
202:       "created": 1709312400,
203:       "member_count": 8,
204:       "task_count": 45,
205:       "archived": false
206:     }
207:   ]
208: }
209: ```
210: 
211: Note that the `created` field here returns a Unix timestamp. We plan to migrate this to ISO 8601 in a future release.
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ### Create Project
216: 
217: **Endpoint:** `POST /api/v2/projects`
218: 
219: To create a new project, send a POST request with the following payload:
220: 
221: ```json
222: {
223:   "name": "My New Project",
224:   "description": "Optional project description"
225: }
226: ```
227: 
228: The `name` field is required and must be unique within the user's organization. Max 100 chars.
229: 
230: **Response fields:**
231: 
232: | Field | Type | Notes |
233: |-------|------|-------|
234: | id | integer | Auto-generated project ID |
235: | name | string | The project name |
236: | description | string | May be null |
237: | owner_id | integer | ID of creating user |
238: | created | integer | Unix timestamp |
239: | member_count | integer | Always 1 for new projects |
240: | task_count | integer | Always 0 for new projects |
241: | archived | boolean | Always false for new projects |
242: 
243: Returns HTTP 201.
244: 
245: No error documentation is provided here but the API follows standard REST conventions for error responses.
246: 
247: ---
248: 
249: ## User Info
250: 
251: ### Getting your profile
252: 
253: **Route**: GET /api/v2/users/me
254: 
255: This returns information about the currently authenticated user. Pass your API key as usual.
256: 
257: The response looks like:
258: 
259: ```json
260: {
261:   "user": {
262:     "id": 57,
263:     "email": "jane@example.com",
264:     "name": "Jane Smith",
265:     "role": "admin",
266:     "organization_id": 5,
267:     "timezone": "America/New_York",
268:     "created_at": "2023-01-15T09:00:00Z",
269:     "last_login": 1709398800
270:   }
271: }
272: ```
273: 
274: Note: `created_at` is ISO 8601 but `last_login` is a Unix timestamp. This inconsistency will be addressed in API v3.
275: 
276: ---
277: 
278: ## Rate Limiting
279: 
280: We enforce rate limits to ensure fair usage of the API. The current limits are:
281: 
282: - 100 requests per minute for free tier
283: - 1000 requests per minute for paid plans
284: 
285: When you exceed the limit, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Check the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header to see how many requests you have left.
286: 
287: ## Pagination
288: 
289: List endpoints support pagination via `page` and `per_page` query parameters. The response `meta` object contains pagination info. Note that the projects endpoint does not currently support pagination - all projects are returned in a single response.
290: 
291: ## Errors
292: 
293: The API uses standard HTTP status codes. Error responses include a JSON body:
294: 
295: ```json
296: {
297:   "error": {
298:     "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
299:     "message": "Title is required",
300:     "details": []
301:   }
302: }
303: ```
304: 
305: However, some older endpoints may return errors in a different format:
306: 
307: ```json
308: {
309:   "error": "not_found",
310:   "message": "Task not found"
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: We are working on standardizing error responses across all routes.
315: 
316: ---
317: 
318: *For questions or support, email api-support@taskflow.io*

1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.
102: 
103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## DELETE /api/projects/:id
114: 
115: Delete a project. All tasks in the project will also be deleted.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Errors
120: 
121: Errors return JSON: `{"error": "message"}`.
122: 
123: Common codes: 400, 401, 404, 500.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Webhooks
128: 
129: POST /api/webhooks - register a webhook. Body: `url`, `events` (array).
130: 
131: GET /api/webhooks - list webhooks.
132: 
133: DELETE /api/webhooks/:id - remove a webhook.
134: 
135: Events: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `project.created`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## Notes
140: 
141: - Rate limit: 60 req/min.
142: - All timestamps are Unix.

1: # RESTAPIDocs Examples
2: 
3: These examples were taken from projects mainly using [Django Rest
4: Framework](https://github.com/tomchristie/django-rest-framework) and so the
5: JSON responses are often similar to the way in which DRF makes responses.
6: 
7: Where full URLs are provided in responses they will be rendered as if service
8: is running on 'http://testserver/'.
9: 
10: ## Open Endpoints
11: 
12: Open endpoints require no Authentication.
13: 
14: * [Login](login.md) : `POST /api/login/`
15: 
16: ## Endpoints that require Authentication
17: 
18: Closed endpoints require a valid Token to be included in the header of the
19: request. A Token can be acquired from the Login view above.
20: 
21: ### Current User related
22: 
23: Each endpoint manipulates or displays information related to the User whose
24: Token is provided with the request:
25: 
26: * [Show info](user/get.md) : `GET /api/user/`
27: * [Update info](user/put.md) : `PUT /api/user/`
28: 
29: ### Account related
30: 
31: Endpoints for viewing and manipulating the Accounts that the Authenticated User
32: has permissions to access.
33: 
34: * [Show Accessible Accounts](accounts/get.md) : `GET /api/accounts/`
35: * [Create Account](accounts/post.md) : `POST /api/accounts/`
36: * [Show An Account](accounts/pk/get.md) : `GET /api/accounts/:pk/`
37: * [Update An Account](accounts/pk/put.md) : `PUT /api/accounts/:pk/`
38: * [Delete An Account](accounts/pk/delete.md) : `DELETE /api/accounts/:pk/`
39: # Show Current User
40: 
41: Get the details of the currently Authenticated User along with basic
42: subscription information.
43: 
44: **URL** : `/api/user/`
45: 
46: **Method** : `GET`
47: 
48: **Auth required** : YES
49: 
50: **Permissions required** : None
51: 
52: ## Success Response
53: 
54: **Code** : `200 OK`
55: 
56: **Content examples**
57: 
58: For a User with ID 1234 on the local database where that User has saved an
59: email address and name information.
60: 
61: ```json
62: {
63:     "id": 1234,
64:     "first_name": "Joe",
65:     "last_name": "Bloggs",
66:     "email": "joe25@example.com"
67: }
68: ```
69: 
70: For a user with ID 4321 on the local database but no details have been set yet.
71: 
72: ```json
73: {
74:     "id": 4321,
75:     "first_name": "",
76:     "last_name": "",
77:     "email": ""
78: }
79: ```
80: 
81: ## Notes
82: 
83: * If the User does not have a `UserInfo` instance when requested then one will
84:   be created for them.
85: 404: Not Found404: Not Found404: Not Found404: Not Found

1: ---
2: stage: none
3: group: unassigned
4: info: For assistance with this Style Guide page, see <https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/product/ux/technical-writing/#assignments-to-other-projects-and-subjects>.
5: description: Writing styles, markup, formatting, and other standards for the GitLab RESTful APIs.
6: title: Documenting REST API resources
7: ---
8: 
9: REST API resources are documented in Markdown under
10: [`/doc/api`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/tree/master/doc/api). Each
11: resource has its own Markdown file, which is linked from
12: [`api_resources.md`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/doc/api/api_resources.md).
13: 
14: When modifying the Markdown or API code, also update the corresponding
15: [OpenAPI definition](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/tree/master/doc/api/openapi), by running
16: `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v2:generate` and `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v3:generate`.
17: To check if the OpenAPI definition needs to be updated, you can run `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v2:check_docs` and
18: `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v3:check_docs`.
19: This is also checked by the `openapi-doc-check` CI/CD job that runs for commits that modify API code or documentation.
20: 
21: The Markdown topic for an API resource must include:
22: 
23: - A block that includes the HTTP method (like GET, PUT, DELETE) followed by the request path. Always start the path with a `/`. For example:
24: 
25:   ```plaintext
26:   GET /api/v4/projects/:id/repository/branches
27:   ```
28: 
29: - A detailed [description of the attributes](#request-attributes).
30: - A detailed [description of the response body](#response-attributes).
31: - A cURL example.
32: - A response body example (in JSON format).
33: 
34: After a new API documentation page is added, [add an entry in the global navigation](site_architecture/global_nav.md#add-a-navigation-entry).
35: 
36: ## Page metadata
37: 
38: When you create a new page, include a `description` metadata field
39: in the front matter that follows these guidelines for consistency:
40: 
41: - Start with "REST API to"
42: - Use action verbs that describe what users can do with the API
43: - Avoid words ending in -ing
44: - Keep to one sentence, ideally under 100 characters
45: - End with a period
46: 
47: For example:
48: 
49: ```yaml
50: ---
51: stage: Example Stage
52: group: Example Group
53: info: To determine the technical writer assigned to the Stage/Group associated with this page, see <https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/product/ux/technical-writing/#assignments>
54: description: REST API to create, update, and delete issues.
55: title: Example page title
56: ---
57: ```
58: 
59: Additional examples:
60: 
61: - `description: REST API to retrieve CI/CD job details, retry and cancel jobs, run manual jobs, and access job logs.`
62: - `description: REST API to create, manage, and monitor CI/CD pipelines.`
63: 
64: ## API topic template
65: 
66: Use the following template to help you get started. Be sure to list any
67: required attributes first in the table.
68: 
69: ````markdown
70: ## API name
71: 
72: {{</* history */>}}
73: 
74: - History note.
75: 
76: {{</* /history */>}}
77: 
78: Use this API to ...
79: 
80: ### Operation title
81: 
82: {{</* history */>}}
83: 
84: - History note.
85: 
86: {{</* /history */>}}
87: 
88: Description of the operation.
89: 
90: ```plaintext
91: METHOD /api/v4/endpoint
92: ```
93: 
94: Supported attributes:
95: 
96: | Attribute                | Type     | Required | Description           |
97: |--------------------------|----------|----------|-----------------------|
98: | `attribute`              | datatype | Yes      | Detailed description. |
99: | `attribute`              | datatype | No       | Detailed description. |
100: | `attribute`              | datatype | No       | Detailed description. |
101: | `attribute`              | datatype | No       | Detailed description. |
102: 
103: If successful, returns [`<status_code>`](rest/troubleshooting.md#status-codes) and the following
104: response attributes:
105: 
106: | Attribute                | Type     | Description           |
107: |--------------------------|----------|-----------------------|
108: | `attribute`              | datatype | Detailed description. |
109: | `attribute`              | datatype | Detailed description. |
110: 
111: Example request:
112: 
113: ```shell
114: curl --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
115:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/endpoint?parameters"
116: ```
117: 
118: Example response:
119: 
120: ```json
121: [
122:   {
123:   }
124: ]
125: ```
126: ````
127: 
128: ## History
129: 
130: Add [history](styleguide/availability_details.md#history)
131: to describe new or updated API calls.
132: 
133: To add history for an individual attribute, include it in the history
134: for the section. For example:
135: 
136: ```markdown
137: ### Edit a widget
138: 
139: {{</* history */>}}
140: 
141:  - `widget_message` [introduced](https://link-to-issue) in GitLab 14.3.
142: 
143: {{</* /history */>}}
144: ```
145: 
146: If the API or attribute is deployed behind a feature flag,
147: [include the feature flag information](feature_flags.md) in the history.
148: 
149: ## Deprecations
150: 
151: To document the deprecation of an API endpoint, follow the steps to
152: [deprecate a page or topic](styleguide/deprecations_and_removals.md).
153: 
154: To deprecate an attribute:
155: 
156: 1. Add a history note.
157: 
158:    ```markdown
159:    {{</* history */>}}
160: 
161:    - `widget_name` [deprecated](https://link-to-issue) in GitLab 14.7.
162: 
163:    {{</* /history */>}}
164:    ```
165: 
166: 1. Add inline deprecation text to the description.
167: 
168:    ```markdown
169:    | Attribute     | Type   | Required | Description |
170:    |---------------|--------|----------|-------------|
171:    | `widget_name` | string | No       | [Deprecated](https://link-to-issue) in GitLab 14.7. Use `widget_id` instead. The name of the widget. |
172:    ```
173: 
174: To widely announce a deprecation, [update the REST API deprecations page](../../api/rest/deprecations.md).
175: 
176: ## API introduction
177: 
178: Each API is made of one or more operations. At the start of the topic, include information that
179: applies to all operations in the API, and a short description of the related features.
180: 
181: For consistency, try to start the introduction with: `Use this API to {verb} + [{feature}](link/to/UI/docs).`
182: This allows us to direct users to related documentation that might include more context.
183: 
184: For example:
185: 
186: - `Use this API to manage [Git branches](path/to/file).`
187: - `Use this API to interact with the [Maven package manager client](path/to/file).`
188: - `Use this API to interact with namespaces, a special resource category used to organize users and groups. For more information, see [namespaces](path/to/file).`
189: 
190: ## Operation titles
191: 
192: Start an operation title with a verb. For consistency,
193: use these verbs based on the HTTP method:
194: 
195: | HTTP method      | Verb     | Alternatives | Examples |
196: | ---------------- | -------- | ------------ | -------- |
197: | `GET` (multiple) | List all |              | `List all group access tokens` |
198: | `GET` (single)   | Retrieve | Download     | `Retrieve a group audit event`, `Download a dependency list export` |
199: | `POST`           | Create   | Add          | `Create a repository branch`, `Add a new emoji reaction` |
200: | `PUT`            | Update   | Replace      | `Update a project topic` |
201: | `PATCH`          | Update   | Modify       | `Update a freeze period`, `Modify an existing commit thread note` |
202: | `DELETE`         | Delete   |              | `Delete a feature` |
203: 
204: When possible, use the recommended verb. Alternatives might be needed in specific contexts, but
205: minimize their use to maintain consistency.
206: 
207: ## Operation descriptions
208: 
209: Each operation should include a short description that explains its use, and highlights any
210: important information. If possible, write the first sentence to broadly repeat the title of
211: the operation. For example:
212: 
213: - `List all project access tokens` -> `Lists all project access tokens.`
214: - `Delete an SSH key` -> `Deletes an SSH key from your user account.`
215: - `Retrieve an enterprise user` -> `Retrieves details on a specified enterprise user.`
216: 
217: ## Request attributes
218: 
219: You must document the request attributes in an operation. When creating the table and attribute descriptions:
220: 
221: - Use the following column names for attribute tables.
222: - List any path attributes first, then any required attributes, then sort alphabetically.
223: - Place the attribute name in code blocks using backticks (`` ` ``).
224: - Document any tier or offering information specific to an attribute in the description.
225:   - If an attribute is available for Premium, mention that it's also available for Ultimate.
226:   - Combine this tier and offering information when possible. For example: `GitLab Self-Managed, Premium and Ultimate only.`
227: 
228: ```markdown
229: | Attribute                    | Type          | Required | Description                                         |
230: |------------------------------|---------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
231: | `title`                      | string        | Yes      | Title of the issue. GitLab Self-Managed only.       |
232: | `assignee_ids`               | integer array | No       | IDs of the users to assign the issue to. Ultimate only. |
233: | `confidential`               | boolean       | No       | Sets the issue to confidential. Default is `false`. |
234: ```
235: 
236: Rendered example:
237: 
238: | Attribute                    | Type          | Required | Description                                         |
239: |------------------------------|---------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
240: | `title`                      | string        | Yes      | Title of the issue. GitLab Self-Managed only.       |
241: | `assignee_ids`               | integer array | No       | IDs of the users to assign the issue to. Ultimate only. |
242: | `confidential`               | boolean       | No       | Sets the issue to confidential. Default is `false`. |
243: 
244: For information about writing attribute descriptions, see the [GraphQL API description style guide](../api_graphql_styleguide.md#description-style-guide).
245: 
246: ### Conditionally required attributes
247: 
248: If an attribute is related to another item, indicate this in the attribute description.
249: 
250: Generally, this happens if one of two attributes is required or if an attribute must be enabled and configured separately.
251: 
252: First define the attribute itself, then mention any requirements. Use this format:
253: 
254:   ```markdown
255:   Required if `attribute1` is `true`.
256:   ```
257: 
258: For example:
259: 
260: | Attribute                  | Type    | Required    | Description |
261: | -------------------------- | ------- | ----------- | ----------- |
262: | `include_saml_users`       | boolean | Conditional | If `true`, returns users with a SAML identity. Required if `include_service_accounts` is `false`. |
263: | `include_service_accounts` | boolean | Conditional | If `true`, returns service account users. Required if `include_saml_users` is `false`. |
264: | `a_related_setting`        | boolean | Conditional | If `true`, does something else. Required if `include_saml_users` is `true`. |
265: 
266: ## Response attributes
267: 
268: You might sometimes need to document the response attributes in an operation. This is not usually required.
269: When creating the table and attribute descriptions:
270: 
271: - Use the following column names for attribute tables.
272: - Sort the table alphabetically.
273: - Place the attribute name in code blocks using backticks (`` ` ``).
274: - If describing an object or array, use dot notation to represent the sub-attributes. For example, `project.name` or `projects[].name`.
275: - Document any tier or offering information specific to an attribute in the description.
276:   - If an attribute is available for Premium, mention that it's also available for Ultimate.
277:   - Combine this tier and offering information when possible. For example: `GitLab Self-Managed, Premium and Ultimate only.`
278: 
279: Start the description with the following sentence, replacing `status code` with the
280: relevant [HTTP status code](../../api/rest/troubleshooting.md#status-codes), for example:
281: 
282: ```markdown
283: If successful, returns [`200 OK`](../../api/rest/troubleshooting.md#status-codes) and the
284: following response attributes:
285: ```
286: 
287: ```markdown
288: | Attribute      | Type          | Description |
289: | -------------- | ------------- | ----------- |
290: | `assignee_ids` | integer array | IDs of the users to assign the issue to. Premium and Ultimate only. |
291: | `commits`      | object array  | Commits in the merge request diff. |
292: | `commits[].id` | string        | ID of the commit. |
293: ```
294: 
295: Rendered example:
296: 
297: | Attribute      | Type          | Description |
298: | -------------- | ------------- | ----------- |
299: | `assignee_ids` | integer array | IDs of the users to assign the issue to. Premium and Ultimate only. |
300: | `commits`      | object array  | Commits in the merge request diff. |
301: | `commits[].id` | string        | ID of the commit. |
302: 
303: For information about writing attribute descriptions, see the [GraphQL API description style guide](../api_graphql_styleguide.md#description-style-guide).
304: 
305: ## cURL commands
306: 
307: - Use `https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/` as an endpoint.
308: - Wherever needed use this personal access token: `<your_access_token>`.
309: - Always put the request first. `GET` is the default so you don't have to
310:   include it.
311: - Use long option names (`--header` instead of `-H`) for legibility. (Tested in
312:   [`scripts/lint-doc.sh`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/scripts/lint-doc.sh).)
313: - Declare URLs with the `--url` parameter, and wrap the URL in double quotes (`"`).
314: - Prefer to use examples using the personal access token and don't pass data of
315:   username and password.
316: - For legibility, use the ` \ ` character and indentation to break long single-line
317:   commands apart into multiple lines.
318: 
319: | Methods                                         | Description                                            |
320: |-------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
321: | `--header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>"` | Use this method as is, whenever authentication needed. |
322: | `--request POST`                                | Use this method when creating new objects.             |
323: | `--request PUT`                                 | Use this method when updating existing objects.        |
324: | `--request DELETE`                              | Use this method when removing existing objects.        |
325: 
326: ## cURL Examples
327: 
328: The following sections include a set of [cURL](https://curl.se/) examples
329: you can use in the API documentation.
330: 
331: > [!warning]
332: > Do not use information for real users, URLs, or tokens. For documentation, refer to our
333: > relevant style guide sections on [fake user information](styleguide/_index.md#fake-user-information),
334: > [fake URLs](styleguide/_index.md#fake-urls), and [fake tokens](styleguide/_index.md#fake-tokens).
335: 
336: ### Simple cURL command
337: 
338: Get the details of a group:
339: 
340: ```shell
341: curl --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
342:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/groups/gitlab-org"
343: ```
344: 
345: ### cURL example with parameters passed in the URL
346: 
347: Create a new project under the authenticated user's namespace:
348: 
349: ```shell
350: curl --request POST --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
351:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects?name=foo"
352: ```
353: 
354: ### Post data using cURL's `--data`
355: 
356: Instead of using `--request POST` and appending the parameters to the URI, you
357: can use cURL's `--data` option. The example below creates a new project
358: `foo` under the authenticated user's namespace.
359:
