Governs every endpoint page produced by the Technical Writing team.\n**Sources of grounding:** The in-house `restapidocs_combined_template.md` endpoint template, the [GitLab REST API documentation guidelines](../task_folder/references/gitlab_api_doc_styleguide.md) snapshot, and the findings recorded in `doc_audit_tracker.csv`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Purpose and scope\n\nThis guide exists because TaskFlow's API documentation was historically written ad-hoc by individual developers. The 2025 documentation audit (`doc_audit_tracker.csv`) found that of 17 audited endpoint rows, 6 required full rewrites, 7 required updates, and only 4 were acceptable as-is. The most common failure modes were not factual errors but *inconsistency*: two reviewers described the same object with different words (\"user\" vs. \"assignee\"), three different formatting styles were used for the same kind of information (tables, bullets, prose), and six pages drifted between active and passive voice.\n\nThis guide eliminates those failures by fixing a single canonical pattern for every endpoint page. If a rule here conflicts with an individual author's preference, this guide wins. If a rule here conflicts with verified product behavior, product behavior wins and this guide must be amended.\n\n## 2. Source-of-truth hierarchy\n\nTaskFlow documents one API from several sources. When sources disagree, resolve them in this order:\n\n1. **The OpenAPI specification** (`taskflow_openapi_v2_extract.yaml`) is the machine-readable contract extracted from the codebase. Parameter names, types, enums, defaults, requiredness, and declared status codes come from the spec.\n2. **Verified production behavior** (delivery logs, trace captures) is authoritative for behavior the spec does not model, such as webhook retry policy. Never publish production-derived behavior without labeling its provenance.\n3. **Prose documentation** is the presentation layer. It may add context, examples, and warnings, but it must never contradict the spec. Any docs-only claim (for example, \"tasks are created in the user's default project when `project_id` is omitted\") that is not backed by the spec must be tagged for engineering verification before publication.\n4. **The audit tracker** is a quality-control instrument, not a source of truth. Its notes reveal gaps that a plain diff of spec versus docs cannot (terminology drift, missing examples, inconsistent formatting). Every row must reach `acceptable` status before the docs it describes may ship.\n\nRule of engagement: **docs may say more than the spec, never less and never differently.** If the spec knows something the docs do not, that is a documentation bug. If the docs know something the spec does not, file a spec-backfill ticket (see §15).\n\n## 3. Page structure\n\nEvery endpoint page follows the combined template's skeleton, hardened with GitLab-style attribute tables. The mandatory order is:\n\n1. **H2 resource section** (for example, `## Tasks`) opening with the sentence pattern `Use this API to <verb> <feature>…`, per the GitLab introduction convention. Example: *\"Use this API to create, read, update, and delete tasks, the primary work units in TaskFlow.\"*\n2. **H3 operation section** per HTTP method. Each operation contains, in order:\n   - Operation title (see §4).\n   - A method-and-path block in a fenced `plaintext` code block, path always beginning with `/`:\n     ```plaintext\n     POST /api/v2/tasks\n     ```\n   - One-sentence description whose first sentence broadly restates the title (GitLab convention: \"List all tasks\" → \"Lists all tasks.\").\n   - Request attributes table (path parameters first, then query/body; required attributes first, then alphabetical). See §5.\n   - Success statement and response attributes, if the response body carries meaningful fields.\n   - Example request (cURL).\n   - Example response (JSON).\n   - Error table.\n3. **Cross-cutting H2 sections** collected once, not repeated per endpoint: Authentication, Rate limiting, Pagination, Errors, Timestamps and formats, Webhook delivery guarantees.\n\nThe page index must list every operation in the form used by the combined template — `* [Operation title](anchor) : `METHOD /path`` — grouped into *Open endpoints* (no auth) and *Endpoints that require authentication*, so readers can orient before diving in.\n\n## 4. Operation titles\n\nStart every operation title with the canonical verb for its HTTP method (adapted from GitLab):\n\n| HTTP method | Verb | Alternatives (use sparingly) | Example |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `GET` (multiple) | List | | **List tasks** |\n| `GET` (single) | Retrieve | Get | **Retrieve a task** |\n| `POST` | Create | Add | **Create a task** |\n| `PUT` | Update | Replace | **Update a task** |\n| `DELETE` | Delete | | **Delete a task** |\n\nForbidden constructions: headings phrased as sentences (\"Updating a task — PUT …\"), gerunds (\"Getting your profile\"), and synonyms that drift by page. The audit tracker flagged exactly this drift: *modify* in one body, *update* in a title; *remove* in a description, *delete* everywhere else. One verb per method, always.\n\n## 5. Attribute tables\n\nAll request and response parameters are documented in Markdown tables, never in bullet lists. The audit tracker shows bullet-list parameters correlate with the lowest completeness scores (40–55%).\n\n**Request columns:** `Attribute | Type | Required | Description`.\n**Response columns:** `Attribute | Type | Description`.\n\nRules:\n\n- Attribute names in backticks. Types use the OpenAPI vocabulary: `string`, `integer`, `boolean`, `string array`, `integer array`, `object`.\n- Path attributes first, then required attributes, then the rest alphabetically.\n- `Required` takes `Yes`, `No`, or `Conditional`. For conditional attributes, define the attribute first, then state the dependency in the canonical form: *\"Required if `mfa_enabled` is `true`.\"*\n- Every attribute gets a meaningful description. Vague stubs (\"The ID\", \"The name\") are audit failures. State defaults as *\"Default is `25`.\"* State enums exhaustively with backticked values, even when a companion table exists.\n- Nullable attributes: state what `null` means — *\"Set to `null` to unassign the task.\"*\n- Nested objects use dot notation in response tables: `meta.current_page`, `data[].assignee_id`.\n\n## 6. Examples\n\nEvery operation carries **at least one cURL example and one JSON response example.** The audit tracker's six `needs_rewrite` rows all lacked one or both.\n\ncURL conventions (GitLab-derived, adapted to TaskFlow):\n\n- Base URL is always `https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/`.\n- Credentials are always the placeholder `<your_api_token>`; never real-looking tokens, emails, or URLs.\n- Use long option names: `--header`, `--request`, `--data`, `--url`. Never `-H`, `-X`, `-d` in reference docs.\n- Always put the URL in `--url \"…\"`. For `GET`, omit `--request` (GET is the default); include `--request` for POST/PUT/DELETE.\n- Break long commands with ` \\` and two-space indentation.\n- Send JSON with an explicit `--header \"Content-Type: application/json\"` and single-quoted `--data '{\"…\"}'`.\n- URL-encode spaces and reserved characters (`%20`, `%2F`).\n\nResponse examples must be realistic, minimal, and consistent with each other: the task with ID `1042`, project `12`, user `57` recur across TaskFlow examples so readers can follow one fixture through the whole document. Show at most two objects in list responses.\n\nLanguage-specific SDK examples (Python, JavaScript) are welcome as *additions* but never as replacements for cURL + JSON.\n\n## 7. Status codes and errors\n\n- Begin the success statement with the GitLab formula: *\"If successful, returns `200 OK` and the following response attributes:\"* (adjust the code: `201 Created`, `204 No Content`).\n- Every operation ends with an error table: `Status code | Meaning | Common causes`. \"The API follows standard REST conventions\" is not documentation; enumerate the codes the spec declares, plus `401` and `429` where relevant.\n- `409 Conflict` must be documented wherever concurrent modification can occur, with recovery guidance (re-`GET`, re-apply, retry).\n- Error bodies: the canonical v2 envelope is\n  ```json\n  { \"error\": { \"code\": \"VALIDATION_ERROR\", \"message\": \"Title is required\", \"details\": [] } }\n  ```\n  Document the legacy flat format (`{\"error\": \"not_found\", \"message\": \"…\"}`) only where it still occurs, and always label it as transitional.\n\n## 8. Voice, tense, and grammar\n\n- Present tense, indicative mood, active voice. The audit tracker's `voice_consistency` column flagged six rows; the fix is mechanical: *\"Retrieves a task\"* not *\"This endpoint can be used to retrieve a task\"* or *\"You can fetch a task.\"*\n- Address the reader as *you*. Never *we* for the API's actions (\"we delete the tasks\") — the API *deletes*.\n- Sentence case for all headings. American spelling. Serial (Oxford) comma.\n- Second person for instructions; third person for system behavior.\n- Do not personify the API. It *returns*, *rejects*, *requires* — it does not *want* or *allow politely*.\n\n## 9. Terminology glossary (canonical terms)\n\nThe audit tracker recorded twelve terminology conflicts. These are now settled:\n\n| ✅ Canonical | ❌ Banned variants | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| retrieve | fetch, get (in prose) | Matches operation titles |\n| endpoint | route, URL (as a noun for an operation) | One noun per concept |\n| task ID | taskId, task_id (in prose) | `taskId` only as a literal path parameter name, in backticks |\n| update | modify, change (as the operation verb) | Verb table in §4 |\n| assignee | user (when discussing assignment) | Distinguishes from actors/watchers |\n| delete | remove | Verb table in §4 |\n| webhook URL | callback URL, destination | One name for the subscriber's endpoint |\n| access token | JWT (in prose) | Implementation detail, not a contract term |\n| token refresh | token rotation | Rotation implies a different algorithm |\n| filter (list endpoints) | query (for list parameters) | Reserve *query* for the search endpoint |\n| request body | payload, body (interchangeably) | Pick one; use *payload* only for webhooks |\n| watcher | follower, observer | Matches `watchers` field name |\n\nWhen a spec field name exists (`assignee_id`, `due_date`), the prose must use it verbatim, in backticks.\n\n## 10. Timestamps and data formats\n\n- The TaskFlow v2 standard is **ISO 8601 UTC**, rendered with a trailing `Z`: `2024-03-01T14:22:00Z`.\n- Known legacy deviations are documented where they occur, with a warning, not silently: project `created` and user `last_login` are Unix timestamps pending normalization (tracked for v3). Never describe a deviation as \"fine\" — describe it, flag it, and give the conversion hint.\n- IDs are integers. Enums are lowercase snake_case (`in_progress`, `task.created`). Dates in *filters* use `YYYY-MM-DD`.\n\n## 11. Webhooks documentation\n\nWebhook events are documented in the published **Webhook Event Catalog** (HTML), which is the single authoritative list. Rules:\n\n- Event names use dot notation `resource.verb` (`task.created`, `member.added`). Never invent synonyms in prose.\n- Every event entry documents: name, description, trigger condition, example payload, and provenance (declared in the OpenAPI spec, observed in the delivery log, or both). Provenance labels are mandatory because the catalog synthesizes contract and production reality; events observed in production but absent from the spec must be marked so integrators do not assume they are subscribable.\n- Document retry behavior with its evidence source. As of the March 2024 export: failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times, then marked `failed`.\n- Document HMAC payload verification whenever `secret` exists on the resource.\n\n## 12. Versioning, history, and deprecation\n\n- Every page carries a version line (`**API version:** 2.0.1`) and a last-reviewed date, mirroring the audit tracker's `last_reviewed` column so the two artifacts stay in lockstep.\n- Additions and behavior changes get a short **History** note at the top of the affected section, in the GitLab pattern: *- `watchers` introduced in TaskFlow API 2.0.*\n- Deprecations are announced in three places: inline in the attribute table (*\"[Deprecated](link) in 2.1. Use `due_date` instead.\"*), in the History note, and on the global deprecations list. Never delete a documented attribute without a replacement pointer.\n\n## 13. Rate limiting and pagination\n\n- Cross-cutting sections state the contract once: tier limits (100 requests/minute free, 1000/minute paid), the `429 Too Many Requests` response, and the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` response header.\n- Pagination parameters are `page` (default `1`) and `per_page` (default `25`, maximum `200`). Any list endpoint that deviates must say so explicitly — the current project list is the known case to watch.\n\n## 14. Accessibility and rendering\n\n- One idea per paragraph; tables over prose for enumerations; fenced code blocks always declare a language (`bash`, `json`, `plaintext`).\n- Warn before destructive operations with a blockquote warning: `> [!warning]` followed by the consequence and any escape hatch (`cascade=false`).\n- Links resolve within the docs set; anchors are GitHub-compatible (lowercase, hyphenated).\n\n## 15. Every operation below conforms to the [TaskFlow API Documentation Style Guide](taskflow_api_style_guide.md); parameters, enums, defaults, and status codes are reconciled against the OpenAPI 3.0 specification (v2.0.1) extracted from the codebase.\n\n## Endpoint index\n\n### Open endpoints\n\n* [Authenticate a user](#authenticate-a-user) : `POST /auth/login`\n* [Refresh an access token](#refresh-an-access-token) : `POST /auth/refresh`\n\n### Endpoints that require authentication\n\n#### Task related\n\n* [List tasks](#list-tasks) : `GET /tasks`\n* [Create a task](#create-a-task) : `POST /tasks`\n* [Retrieve a task](#retrieve-a-task) : `GET /tasks/{taskId}`\n* [Update a task](#update-a-task) : `PUT /tasks/{taskId}`\n* [Delete a task](#delete-a-task) : `DELETE /tasks/{taskId}`\n* [Assign a task](#assign-a-task) : `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign`\n\n#### Project related\n\n* [List projects](#list-projects) : `GET /projects`\n* [Create a project](#create-a-project) : `POST /projects`\n* [Retrieve a project](#retrieve-a-project) : `GET /projects/{projectId}`\n* [Update a project](#update-a-project) : `PUT /projects/{projectId}`\n* [Delete a project](#delete-a-project) : `DELETE /projects/{projectId}`\n\n#### User related\n\n* [Retrieve the current user](#retrieve-the-current-user) : `GET /users/me`\n\n#### Webhook related\n\n* [Create a webhook](#create-a-webhook) : `POST /webhooks`\n* [Delete a webhook](#delete-a-webhook) : `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}`\n\n#### Search related\n\n* [Search tasks](#search-tasks) : `GET /search/tasks`\n\n---\n\n## Authentication\n\nTaskFlow v2 supports two credential types. Include either one in the `Authorization` header of every request to a protected endpoint:\n\n```plaintext\nAuthorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\n```\n\n1. **Static API tokens.** Generate a long-lived API token from the TaskFlow dashboard under **Settings > API Keys**. Use these for server-to-server integrations that do not act on behalf of an individual user.\n2. **Login token pairs.** Exchange a user's credentials for an access token and a refresh token with [`POST /auth/login`](#authenticate-a-user). Access tokens are short-lived; renew them with [`POST /auth/refresh`](#refresh-an-access-token). Use these for integrations that act on behalf of a user.\n\nIf credentials are missing, malformed, or expired, the API returns `401 Unauthorized` in the [standard error format](#errors).\n\n### Authenticate a user\n\nExchanges an email address and password for an access token and refresh token.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/auth/login\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute    | Type   | Required | Description                                                                 |\n|--------------|--------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `email`      | string | Yes      | The user's email address.                                                   |\n| `password`   | string | Yes      | The user's password.                                                        |\n| `mfa_code`   | string | Conditional | Time-based one-time code. Required if MFA is enabled on the account.     |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with a token pair:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"access_token\": \"at_9f2c...\",\n  \"refresh_token\": \"rt_1a8e...\",\n  \"token_type\": \"Bearer\",\n  \"expires_in\": 3600\n}\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning              | Common causes                                                        |\n|-------------|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Invalid credentials  | Unknown email, wrong password.                                       |\n| `403`       | MFA required         | MFA is enabled on the account and `mfa_code` was absent or invalid.  |\n\n### Refresh an access token\n\nExchanges a valid refresh token for a new token pair.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/auth/refresh\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute       | Type   | Required | Description                          |\n|-----------------|--------|----------|--------------------------------------|\n| `refresh_token` | string | Yes      | The refresh token issued by login.   |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` and a new token pair (same shape as the login response).\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                             | Common causes                                    |\n|-------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Refresh token expired or revoked    | Token older than its validity window, or rotated/revoked by logout. |\n\n---\n\n## Tasks\n\nUse this API to create, retrieve, update, and delete tasks, the primary work units in TaskFlow.\n\n### List tasks\n\nLists all tasks the authenticated user can access, with filtering, sorting, and pagination.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/tasks\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute    | Type    | Required | Description                                                                        |\n|--------------|---------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `status`     | string  | No       | Filter by task status. One of `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived`, `blocked`.|\n| `project_id` | integer | No       | Only return tasks belonging to this project.                                       |\n| `page`       | integer | No       | Page number to return. Default is `1`.                                             |\n| `per_page`   | integer | No       | Number of results per page. Default is `25`. Maximum is `200`.                     |\n| `sort`       | string  | No       | Sort field. One of `created_at`, `updated_at`, `priority`, `due_date`.             |\n| `order`      | string  | No       | Sort direction. One of `asc`, `desc`.                                              |\n| `label`      | string  | No       | Filter tasks by label name.                                                        |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` and a paginated envelope with the following response attributes:\n\n| Attribute           | Type          | Description                              |\n|---------------------|---------------|------------------------------------------|\n| `data`              | object array  | The page of task objects.                |\n| `data[].id`         | integer       | Task ID.                                 |\n| `data[].title`      | string        | Task title.                              |\n| `data[].status`     | string        | Task status.                             |\n| `data[].priority`   | string        | Task priority.                           |\n| `meta.current_page` | integer       | Page number returned.                    |\n| `meta.total_pages`  | integer       | Total number of pages available.         |\n| `meta.total_count`  | integer       | Total number of matching tasks.          |\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks?status=open&page=1\"\n```\n\nExample response:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"data\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": 1042,\n      \"title\": \"Fix login bug\",\n      \"description\": \"Users are unable to login with SSO\",\n      \"status\": \"open\",\n      \"priority\": \"high\",\n      \"assignee_id\": 57,\n      \"project_id\": 12,\n      \"created_at\": \"2024-03-01T14:22:00Z\",\n      \"updated_at\": \"2024-03-01T14:22:00Z\",\n      \"due_date\": \"2024-03-15T00:00:00Z\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"meta\": {\n    \"current_page\": 1,\n    \"total_pages\": 5,\n    \"total_count\": 98\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning              | Common causes                          |\n|-------------|----------------------|----------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized         | Missing or invalid token.              |\n| `429`       | Too Many Requests    | Rate limit exceeded. See [Rate limiting](#rate-limiting). |\n\n### Create a task\n\nCreates a task. Only `title` is required; all other attributes are optional.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/tasks\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute      | Type          | Required | Description                                                                     |\n|----------------|---------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `title`        | string        | Yes      | Title of the task. Maximum 200 characters.                                      |\n| `description`  | string        | No       | Longer description. Supports Markdown formatting.                               |\n| `status`       | string        | No       | Initial status. Default is `open`.                                              |\n| `priority`     | string        | No       | One of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`, `urgent`.                           |\n| `assignee_id`  | integer       | No       | ID of the user to assign the task to.                                           |\n| `project_id`   | integer       | No       | Project to create the task in. If omitted, the task is placed in the user's default project *(behavior pending engineering verification)*. |\n| `due_date`     | string        | No       | Due date. ISO 8601 date-time (`2024-04-01T00:00:00Z`).                          |\n| `tags`         | string array  | No       | Tags to apply to the task.                                                      |\n| `watchers`     | integer array | No       | User IDs to add as watchers.                                                    |\n\nIf successful, returns `201 Created` with the full task object.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request POST \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\n    \"title\": \"Design new landing page\",\n    \"description\": \"Create mockups for the Q2 marketing campaign\",\n    \"priority\": \"high\",\n    \"project_id\": 12,\n    \"due_date\": \"2024-04-01T00:00:00Z\",\n    \"tags\": [\"design\", \"marketing\"],\n    \"watchers\": [57, 82]\n  }' \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks\"\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning            | Common causes                                             |\n|-------------|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|\n| `400`       | Bad request        | Malformed JSON body.                                      |\n| `401`       | Unauthorized       | Missing or invalid token.                                 |\n| `422`       | Validation error   | `title` missing or longer than 200 characters; invalid enum value. |\n\n### Retrieve a task\n\nRetrieves a single task by its ID.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute  | Type    | Required | Description                                                                                      |\n|------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `taskId`   | integer | Yes      | ID of the task to retrieve.                                                                      |\n| `include`  | string  | No       | Expand related resources in the response. One of `comments`, `history`, `attachments`.           |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with the full task object (same schema as the list endpoint), plus the requested related resources when `include` is supplied.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042?include=comments\"\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning       | Common causes                                        |\n|-------------|---------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized  | Missing or invalid token.                            |\n| `404`       | Task not found| Task does not exist or you do not have access to it. |\n\n### Update a task\n\nUpdates a task. Partial updates are supported: send only the fields you want to change; omitted fields remain unchanged. `id` and `created_at` cannot be modified.\n\n```plaintext\nPUT /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute      | Type          | Required | Description                                                        |\n|----------------|---------------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `taskId`       | integer       | Yes      | ID of the task to update.                                          |\n| `title`        | string        | No       | New title.                                                         |\n| `description`  | string        | No       | New description.                                                   |\n| `status`       | string        | No       | Must be a valid status string.                                     |\n| `priority`     | string        | No       | One of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`, `urgent`.              |\n| `assignee_id`  | integer       | No       | Assignee's user ID. Set to `null` to unassign.                     |\n| `project_id`   | integer       | No       | Move the task to this project.                                     |\n| `due_date`     | string        | No       | ISO 8601 date-time. Set to `null` to clear.                        |\n| `tags`         | string array  | No       | Replace the task's tags.                                           |\n| `watchers`     | integer array | No       | Replace the task's watcher user IDs.                               |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` and the updated task object.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request PUT \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\"status\": \"in_progress\", \"assignee_id\": 57}' \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042\"\n```\n\nExample response:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 1042,\n  \"title\": \"Fix login bug\",\n  \"status\": \"in_progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"high\",\n  \"assignee_id\": 57,\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"updated_at\": \"2024-03-02T10:15:00Z\"\n}\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning      | Common causes                                                            |\n|-------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid token.                                                |\n| `404`       | Task not found | Task does not exist or you do not have access to it.                   |\n| `409`       | Conflict     | Concurrent modification detected: the task changed since you last read it. Re-fetch the task, re-apply your change, and retry. |\n\n### Delete a task\n\nDeletes a task permanently. This action cannot be undone.\n\n```plaintext\nDELETE /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute | Type    | Required | Description               |\n|-----------|---------|----------|---------------------------|\n| `taskId`  | integer | Yes      | ID of the task to delete. |\n\nPermissions: you must be an admin or owner on the project that contains the task. Regular members can delete only tasks they created.\n\nIf successful, returns `204 No Content`. The response body is empty.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request DELETE \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042\"\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning         | Common causes                                   |\n|-------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------------------|\n| `403`       | Forbidden       | Insufficient permissions on the project.        |\n| `404`       | Task not found  | Task does not exist or you do not have access.  |\n\n### Assign a task\n\nAssigns a task to an assignee. Use this operation instead of `PUT /tasks/{taskId}` when the only change is assignment, because it additionally triggers assignment notifications.\n\nReassignment behavior: assigning a task that already has an assignee replaces the existing assignee. The previous assignee loses assignment notifications; watchers are unaffected.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}/assign\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute     | Type    | Required | Description                                                      |\n|---------------|---------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `taskId`      | integer | Yes      | ID of the task to assign.                                        |\n| `assignee_id` | integer | Yes      | ID of the user to assign the task to.                            |\n| `notify`      | boolean | No       | Whether to send a notification to the assignee. Default is `true`. |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with the assigned task object.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request POST \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\"assignee_id\": 93, \"notify\": true}' \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1050/assign\"\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning              | Common causes                                       |\n|-------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized         | Missing or invalid token.                           |\n| `404`       | Task or user not found | `taskId` or `assignee_id` does not exist, or you lack access. |\n\n---\n\n## Projects\n\nUse this API to manage projects, the containers that organize tasks and members.\n\n### List projects\n\nLists all projects the authenticated user has access to. Projects are returned in alphabetical order by name *(ordering pending engineering verification)*.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/projects\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute  | Type    | Required | Description                                                            |\n|------------|---------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `archived` | boolean | No       | If `true`, include archived projects. Default is `false`.              |\n| `role`     | string  | No       | Filter by your role in the project. One of `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `viewer`. |\n| `page`     | integer | No       | Page number to return.                                                 |\n| `per_page` | integer | No       | Number of results per page.                                            |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with a `projects` array.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects?archived=false\"\n```\n\nExample response:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"projects\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": 12,\n      \"name\": \"Website Redesign\",\n      \"description\": \"Q2 2024 website overhaul\",\n      \"owner_id\": 57,\n      \"created\": 1709312400,\n      \"member_count\": 8,\n      \"task_count\": 45,\n      \"archived\": false\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n> [!warning]\n> The `created` field is a Unix timestamp, not ISO 8601. This is a known legacy deviation; the TaskFlow timestamp standard is ISO 8601 UTC (see [Timestamps](#timestamps-and-formats)) and this field is scheduled to migrate in a future release.\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning      | Common causes             |\n|-------------|--------------|---------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid token. |\n\n### Create a project\n\nCreates a project. `name` is required and must be unique within your organization, with a maximum of 100 characters.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/projects\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute      | Type   | Required | Description                                                                       |\n|----------------|--------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `name`         | string | Yes      | Project name. Maximum 100 characters; unique within the organization.             |\n| `description`  | string | No       | Optional project description.                                                     |\n| `template_id`  | integer| No       | Create from an existing project template.                                         |\n| `visibility`   | string | No       | One of `private`, `internal`, `public`. Default is `private`.                     |\n\nIf successful, returns `201 Created` with the new project object (same fields as the list endpoint; `member_count` is `1`, `task_count` is `0`, and `archived` is `false` for new projects).\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request POST \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\"name\": \"My New Project\", \"visibility\": \"internal\"}' \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects\"\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning            | Common causes                                        |\n|-------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| `400`       | Bad request        | Malformed JSON body.                                 |\n| `401`       | Unauthorized       | Missing or invalid token.                            |\n| `422`       | Validation error   | `name` missing, longer than 100 characters, or not unique. |\n\n### Retrieve a project\n\nRetrieves a single project by its ID.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute   | Type    | Required | Description                    |\n|-------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------|\n| `projectId` | integer | Yes      | ID of the project to retrieve. |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with the project object.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/12\"\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning          | Common causes                                      |\n|-------------|------------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized     | Missing or invalid token.                          |\n| `404`       | Project not found| Project does not exist or you do not have access.  |\n\n### Update a project\n\nUpdates a project. Partial updates are supported: send only the fields you want to change.\n\n```plaintext\nPUT /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute     | Type    | Required | Description                                        |\n|---------------|---------|----------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `projectId`   | integer | Yes      | ID of the project to update.                       |\n| `name`        | string  | No       | New project name.                                  |\n| `description` | string  | No       | New project description.                           |\n| `archived`    | boolean | No       | Set to `true` to archive the project.              |\n| `visibility`  | string  | No       | One of `private`, `internal`, `public`.            |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` and the updated project object.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request PUT \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\"description\": \"Q2 2024 website overhaul - updated scope\"}' \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/12\"\n```\n\nExample response:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 12,\n  \"name\": \"Website Redesign\",\n  \"description\": \"Q2 2024 website overhaul - updated scope\",\n  \"owner_id\": 57,\n  \"archived\": false\n}\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning           | Common causes                                     |\n|-------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized      | Missing or invalid token.                         |\n| `404`       | Project not found | Project does not exist or you do not have access. |\n\n### Delete a project\n\nDeletes a project permanently. This action cannot be undone.\n\n```plaintext\nDELETE /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute   | Type    | Required | Description                                                        |\n|-------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `projectId` | integer | Yes      | ID of the project to delete.                                       |\n| `cascade`   | boolean | No       | If `true`, deletes all tasks within the project. Default is `true`.|\n\n> [!warning]\n> By default, deleting a project also deletes every task in it. Pass `cascade=false` to keep the tasks.\n\nIf successful, returns `204 No Content`. The response body is empty.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request DELETE \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/12?cascade=false\"\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning           | Common causes                                     |\n|-------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized      | Missing or invalid token.                         |\n| `403`       | Forbidden         | Insufficient permissions on the project.          |\n| `404`       | Project not found | Project does not exist or you do not have access. |\n\n---\n\n## Users\n\nUse this API to retrieve information about the authenticated user.\n\n### Retrieve the current user\n\nRetrieves the profile of the currently authenticated user.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/users/me\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute | Type   | Required | Description                                                        |\n|-----------|--------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `fields`  | string | No       | Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response.         |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with the user object.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/users/me?fields=id,email,name,timezone\"\n```\n\nExample response:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user\": {\n    \"id\": 57,\n    \"email\": \"jane@example.com\",\n    \"name\": \"Jane Smith\",\n    \"role\": \"admin\",\n    \"organization_id\": 5,\n    \"timezone\": \"America/New_York\",\n    \"created_at\": \"2023-01-15T09:00:00Z\",\n    \"last_login\": 1709398800\n  }\n}\n```\n\n> [!warning]\n> `created_at` is ISO 8601 but `last_login` is a Unix timestamp. This legacy deviation will be addressed in API v3.\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning      | Common causes             |\n|-------------|--------------|---------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid token. |\n\n---\n\n## Webhooks\n\nUse this API to manage webhooks, which deliver real-time event notifications to your integration endpoints. The complete list of event types, trigger conditions, payload examples, and provenance is maintained in the [Webhook Event Catalog](webhook_event_catalog.html).\n\n### Create a webhook\n\nCreates a webhook that delivers the selected event types to your webhook URL.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/webhooks\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute | Type          | Required | Description                                                                 |\n|-----------|---------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `url`     | string (URI)  | Yes      | The webhook URL that receives event deliveries.                             |\n| `events`  | string array  | Yes      | Event types to subscribe to. Default is `true`.                     |\n\nIf successful, returns `201 Created` with the created webhook object.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request POST \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\n    \"url\": \"https://integrations.acme.corp/taskflow/events\",\n    \"events\": [\"task.created\", \"task.updated\", \"task.assigned\"],\n    \"secret\": \"<your_hmac_secret>\",\n    \"active\": true\n  }' \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/webhooks\"\n```\n\n**Delivery guarantees.** Failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times; if every attempt fails, the delivery is marked `failed` (evidence: production delivery log, March 2024 export — delivery `d-90008`, HTTP 502, `retry_attempts: 3`, `final_status: failed`). Verify payload authenticity by computing an HMAC with your `secret` over the raw request body.\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning          | Common causes                              |\n|-------------|------------------|--------------------------------------------|\n| `400`       | Bad request      | Malformed JSON body.                       |\n| `401`       | Unauthorized     | Missing or invalid token.                  |\n| `422`       | Validation error | `url` is not a valid URI, or `events` contains an unknown event type. |\n\n### Delete a webhook\n\nDeletes a webhook permanently. The webhook URL stops receiving deliveries immediately; this action cannot be undone.\n\n```plaintext\nDELETE /api/v2/webhooks/{webhookId}\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute   | Type    | Required | Description                    |\n|-------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------|\n| `webhookId` | integer | Yes      | ID of the webhook to delete.   |\n\nIf successful, returns `204 No Content`. The response body is empty.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request DELETE \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/webhooks/301\"\n```\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning           | Common causes                                     |\n|-------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------|\n| `401`       | Unauthorized      | Missing or invalid token.                         |\n| `404`       | Webhook not found | Webhook does not exist or you do not own it.      |\n\n---\n\n## Search\n\nUse this API to find tasks by text and attribute filters.\n\n### Search tasks\n\nSearches tasks with a full-text query, optionally scoped by project, status, and date range.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/search/tasks\n```\n\nSupported attributes:\n\n| Attribute    | Type    | Required | Description                                     |\n|--------------|---------|----------|-------------------------------------------------|\n| `q`          | string  | Yes      | Full-text search query.                         |\n| `project_id` | integer | No       | Restrict results to this project.               |\n| `status`     | string  | No       | Restrict results to this task status.           |\n| `date_from`  | string  | No       | Lower bound (inclusive) on task dates. `YYYY-MM-DD`. |\n| `date_to`    | string  | No       | Upper bound (inclusive) on task dates. `YYYY-MM-DD`. |\n\nIf successful, returns `200 OK` with matching task objects.\n\nExample request:\n\n```bash\ncurl --request GET \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_api_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/search/tasks?q=landing%20page&project_id=12\"\n```\n\n> [!note]\n> Advanced query syntax (operators, field-scoped terms) is supported only partially and is not yet fully specified. Contact API support before relying on operator behavior.\n\n**Errors**\n\n| Status code | Meaning      | Common causes                                        |\n|-------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| `400`       | Bad request  | `q` missing or invalid filter combination.           |\n| `401`       | Unauthorized | Missing or invalid token.                            |\n\n---\n\n## Rate limiting\n\nThe API enforces rate limits to ensure fair usage:\n\n- **Free tier:** 100 requests per minute.\n- **Paid plans:** 1000 requests per minute.\n\nWhen you exceed the limit, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Check the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` response header to see how many requests you have left, and back off before retrying.\n\n## Pagination\n\nList endpoints support pagination via `page` and `per_page` query parameters. The response `meta` object contains pagination info (`current_page`, `total_pages`, `total_count`). The projects endpoint also accepts `page` and `per_page` per the OpenAPI specification; the earlier statement that it does not paginate was an error and has been removed.\n\n## Errors\n\nThe API uses standard HTTP status codes. The canonical v2 error body is:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": \"VALIDATION_ERROR\",\n    \"message\": \"Title is required\",\n    \"details\": []\n  }\n}\n```\n\nSome older endpoints may still return the legacy format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"error\": \"not_found\",\n  \"message\": \"Task not found\"\n}\n```\n\nTreat the canonical envelope as the contract for new integrations. The legacy format is transitional and will be removed.\n\n## Timestamps and formats\n\n- All request and response timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with a trailing `Z` (for example, `2024-03-01T14:22:00Z`), except the known legacy Unix-timestamp fields: project `created` and user `last_login`. Both are flagged at their endpoints and are scheduled to migrate.\n- IDs are integers. Enum values are lowercase snake_case.\n\n## Changelog summary (docs reconciliation)\n\nThis reference was reconciled against the OpenAPI v2.0.1 spec and the documentation audit tracker. Highlights of what changed versus the previous ad-hoc docs:\n\n- Added the missing auth flow (`POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`) with MFA handling.\n- Corrected task `title` maximum length (255 → 200), `per_page` defaults (20/100 → 25/200), and the `status`/`priority`/`sort` enums (`blocked`, `urgent`, `due_date` added).\n- Documented `label` filtering and the `include` expansion parameter on task retrieval.\n- Documented `watchers`, `409 Conflict` on task update, and the assign operation with `notify`.\n- Documented project pagination (previously wrongly denied), `template_id`, `visibility`, project update and delete operations, and the `cascade` delete behavior.\n- Documented the `fields` parameter on `GET /users/me`.\n- Added full webhook and search reference sections, retry guarantees, and HMAC verification guidance.\n\n*For questions or support, email api-support@taskflow.io.*\n"}", "type": "tool_call"}], "finish_reason": "tool_calls"}]}}, "weave": {"client_version": "0.1.0b0", "source": "coreweave-forge-sdk", "sys_version": "3.12.13 (main, Jun 23 2026, 15:44:24) [Clang 22.1.3 ]", "os_name": "Darwin", "os_version": "Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0: Tue Aug 18 17:51:47 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.161.15.700.19~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6050", "os_release": "25.6.0"}}, "events": [], "links": [], "resource": {"attributes": {"telemetry": {"sdk": {"language": "python", "name": "opentelemetry", "version": "1.45.1"}}, "service": {"instance": {"id": "212b1610-5725-4f59-80e6-fb049e944d22"}, "name": "harness2-showcase"}, "wandb": {"sdk": {"name": "forge", "version": "0.1.0b0", "language": "python"}, "entity": "wandb", "project": "harness2-agent-lens"}}, "dropped_attributes_count": 0}}

1: # TaskFlow API Documentation
2: 
3: **Version**: 2.0
4: **Last Updated**: March 2024
5: 
6: Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.
7: 
8: ## Authentication
9: 
10: All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:
11: 
12: ```
13: Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
14: ```
15: 
16: You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## Tasks
21: 
22: ### GET /api/v2/tasks
23: 
24: Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.
25: 
26: **Query Parameters**
27: 
28: | Parameter | Type | Description |
29: |-----------|------|-------------|
30: | status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |
31: | project_id | integer | Only return tasks belonging to this project |
32: | page | integer | Page number for pagination (default: 1) |
33: | per_page | integer | Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 100) |
34: | sort | string | Sort field. One of `created_at`, `updated_at`, `priority` |
35: | order | string | Sort direction: `asc` or `desc` |
36: 
37: **Example Request**
38: 
39: ```bash
40: curl -X GET "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks?status=open&page=1" \
41:   -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
42: ```
43: 
44: **Response** (200 OK)
45: 
46: ```json
47: {
48:   "data": [
49:     {
50:       "id": 1042,
51:       "title": "Fix login bug",
52:       "description": "Users are unable to login with SSO",
53:       "status": "open",
54:       "priority": "high",
55:       "assignee_id": 57,
56:       "project_id": 12,
57:       "created_at": "2024-03-01T14:22:00Z",
58:       "updated_at": "2024-03-01T14:22:00Z",
59:       "due_date": "2024-03-15T00:00:00Z"
60:     }
61:   ],
62:   "meta": {
63:     "current_page": 1,
64:     "total_pages": 5,
65:     "total_count": 98
66:   }
67: }
68: ```
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ### POST /api/v2/tasks
73: 
74: Creates a new task. You must provide at least a title. The task will be created under the user's default project if `project_id` is not specified.
75: 
76: **Request Body Arguments**
77: 
78: - `title` (string, **required**) - The title of the task. Max 255 characters.
79: - `description` (string) - A longer description. Supports Markdown formatting.
80: - `status` (string) - Initial status. Defaults to `open`.
81: - `priority` (string) - One of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`. Default is `medium`.
82: - `assignee_id` (integer) - User ID to assign the task to.
83: - `project_id` (integer) - Project to create the task in.
84: - `due_date` (string) - Due date in ISO 8601 format.
85: - `tags` (array of strings) - Tags to apply to the task.
86: 
87: **Example**
88: 
89: ```python
90: import requests
91: 
92: resp = requests.post(
93:     "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks",
94:     headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"},
95:     json={
96:         "title": "Design new landing page",
97:         "description": "Create mockups for the Q2 marketing campaign",
98:         "priority": "high",
99:         "project_id": 12,
100:         "due_date": "2024-04-01T00:00:00Z",
101:         "tags": ["design", "marketing"]
102:     }
103: )
104: print(resp.json())
105: ```
106: 
107: Returns `201 Created` on success with the full task object in the response body.
108: 
109: **Errors**
110: 
111: | Status Code | Meaning |
112: |------------|---------|
113: | 400 | Bad request - missing required fields or invalid values |
114: | 401 | Authentication failed |
115: | 422 | Validation error (e.g. title too long) |
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ### GET /api/v2/tasks/{id}
120: 
121: Get a single task by its ID.
122: 
123: Pass the task ID as a path parameter. Returns the task object if found. Returns 404 if the task doesn't exist or you don't have access.
124: 
125: Response includes the full task object (same schema as list endpoint).
126: 
127: No additional arguments.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ### Updating a task - PUT /api/v2/tasks/{id}
132: 
133: We support partial updates - you only need to send the fields you want to change. Any fields not included in the request body will remain unchanged.
134: 
135: Note: the `id` and `created_at` fields cannot be modified.
136: 
137: **Fields you can update:**
138: 
139: - title
140: - description
141: - status (must be a valid status string)
142: - priority
143: - assignee_id (set to `null` to unassign)
144: - project_id
145: - due_date (ISO 8601 timestamp or null to clear)
146: - tags
147: 
148: **Sample curl command:**
149: 
150: ```bash
151: curl -X PUT "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042" \
152:   -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
153:   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
154:   -d '{"status": "in_progress", "assignee_id": 57}'
155: ```
156: 
157: The API returns `200 OK` and the updated task object on success.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ### DELETE /api/v2/tasks/{id}
162: 
163: Permanently deletes a task. This action cannot be undone.
164: 
165: The user must have admin or owner permissions on the project that the task belongs to. Regular members can only delete tasks they created.
166: 
167: **Returns:**
168: 
169: `204 No Content` on success. The response body is empty.
170: 
171: If the task is not found a `404` error is returned. Attempting to delete a task without sufficient permissions results in `403 Forbidden`.
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## Projects
176: 
177: ### List projects
178: 
179: ```
180: GET /api/v2/projects
181: ```
182: 
183: This route returns all projects the authenticated user has access to. Projects are returned in alphabetical order by name.
184: 
185: **Query args:**
186: 
187: - `archived` (boolean) - if `true`, include archived projects. Default `false`.
188: - `role` (string) - filter by the user's role in the project: `owner`, `admin`, `member`
189: 
190: No authentication header examples are given here since it follows the same pattern described at the top of this doc.
191: 
192: **Sample response:**
193: 
194: ```json
195: {
196:   "projects": [
197:     {
198:       "id": 12,
199:       "name": "Website Redesign",
200:       "description": "Q2 2024 website overhaul",
201:       "owner_id": 57,
202:       "created": 1709312400,
203:       "member_count": 8,
204:       "task_count": 45,
205:       "archived": false
206:     }
207:   ]
208: }
209: ```
210: 
211: Note that the `created` field here returns a Unix timestamp. We plan to migrate this to ISO 8601 in a future release.
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ### Create Project
216: 
217: **Endpoint:** `POST /api/v2/projects`
218: 
219: To create a new project, send a POST request with the following payload:
220: 
221: ```json
222: {
223:   "name": "My New Project",
224:   "description": "Optional project description"
225: }
226: ```
227: 
228: The `name` field is required and must be unique within the user's organization. Max 100 chars.
229: 
230: **Response fields:**
231: 
232: | Field | Type | Notes |
233: |-------|------|-------|
234: | id | integer | Auto-generated project ID |
235: | name | string | The project name |
236: | description | string | May be null |
237: | owner_id | integer | ID of creating user |
238: | created | integer | Unix timestamp |
239: | member_count | integer | Always 1 for new projects |
240: | task_count | integer | Always 0 for new projects |
241: | archived | boolean | Always false for new projects |
242: 
243: Returns HTTP 201.
244: 
245: No error documentation is provided here but the API follows standard REST conventions for error responses.
246: 
247: ---
248: 
249: ## User Info
250: 
251: ### Getting your profile
252: 
253: **Route**: GET /api/v2/users/me
254: 
255: This returns information about the currently authenticated user. Pass your API key as usual.
256: 
257: The response looks like:
258: 
259: ```json
260: {
261:   "user": {
262:     "id": 57,
263:     "email": "jane@example.com",
264:     "name": "Jane Smith",
265:     "role": "admin",
266:     "organization_id": 5,
267:     "timezone": "America/New_York",
268:     "created_at": "2023-01-15T09:00:00Z",
269:     "last_login": 1709398800
270:   }
271: }
272: ```
273: 
274: Note: `created_at` is ISO 8601 but `last_login` is a Unix timestamp. This inconsistency will be addressed in API v3.
275: 
276: ---
277: 
278: ## Rate Limiting
279: 
280: We enforce rate limits to ensure fair usage of the API. The current limits are:
281: 
282: - 100 requests per minute for free tier
283: - 1000 requests per minute for paid plans
284: 
285: When you exceed the limit, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Check the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header to see how many requests you have left.
286: 
287: ## Pagination
288: 
289: List endpoints support pagination via `page` and `per_page` query parameters. The response `meta` object contains pagination info. Note that the projects endpoint does not currently support pagination - all projects are returned in a single response.
290: 
291: ## Errors
292: 
293: The API uses standard HTTP status codes. Error responses include a JSON body:
294: 
295: ```json
296: {
297:   "error": {
298:     "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
299:     "message": "Title is required",
300:     "details": []
301:   }
302: }
303: ```
304: 
305: However, some older endpoints may return errors in a different format:
306: 
307: ```json
308: {
309:   "error": "not_found",
310:   "message": "Task not found"
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: We are working on standardizing error responses across all routes.
315: 
316: ---
317: 
318: *For questions or support, email api-support@taskflow.io*

(End of file - total 318 lines)

1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.
102: 
103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## DELETE /api/projects/:id
114: 
115: Delete a project. All tasks in the project will also be deleted.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Errors
120: 
121: Errors return JSON: `{"error": "message"}`.
122: 
123: Common codes: 400, 401, 404, 500.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Webhooks
128: 
129: POST /api/webhooks - register a webhook. Body: `url`, `events` (array).
130: 
131: GET /api/webhooks - list webhooks.
132: 
133: DELETE /api/webhooks/:id - remove a webhook.
134: 
135: Events: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `project.created`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## Notes
140: 
141: - Rate limit: 60 req/min.
142: - All timestamps are Unix.
143: - Contact support@taskflow.io for help.

(End of file - total 143 lines)
</content>", "type": "text"}]

1: # RESTAPIDocs Examples
2: 
3: These examples were taken from projects mainly using [Django Rest
4: Framework](https://github.com/tomchristie/django-rest-framework) and so the
5: JSON responses are often similar to the way in which DRF makes responses.
6: 
7: Where full URLs are provided in responses they will be rendered as if service
8: is running on 'http://testserver/'.
9: 
10: ## Open Endpoints
11: 
12: Open endpoints require no Authentication.
13: 
14: * [Login](login.md) : `POST /api/login/`
15: 
16: ## Endpoints that require Authentication
17: 
18: Closed endpoints require a valid Token to be included in the header of the
19: request. A Token can be acquired from the Login view above.
20: 
21: ### Current User related
22: 
23: Each endpoint manipulates or displays information related to the User whose
24: Token is provided with the request:
25: 
26: * [Show info](user/get.md) : `GET /api/user/`
27: * [Update info](user/put.md) : `PUT /api/user/`
28: 
29: ### Account related
30: 
31: Endpoints for viewing and manipulating the Accounts that the Authenticated User
32: has permissions to access.
33: 
34: * [Show Accessible Accounts](accounts/get.md) : `GET /api/accounts/`
35: * [Create Account](accounts/post.md) : `POST /api/accounts/`
36: * [Show An Account](accounts/pk/get.md) : `GET /api/accounts/:pk/`
37: * [Update An Account](accounts/pk/put.md) : `PUT /api/accounts/:pk/`
38: * [Delete An Account](accounts/pk/delete.md) : `DELETE /api/accounts/:pk/`
39: # Show Current User
40: 
41: Get the details of the currently Authenticated User along with basic
42: subscription information.
43: 
44: **URL** : `/api/user/`
45: 
46: **Method** : `GET`
47: 
48: **Auth required** : YES
49: 
50: **Permissions required** : None
51: 
52: ## Success Response
53: 
54: **Code** : `200 OK`
55: 
56: **Content examples**
57: 
58: For a User with ID 1234 on the local database where that User has saved an
59: email address and name information.
60: 
61: ```json
62: {
63:     "id": 1234,
64:     "first_name": "Joe",
65:     "last_name": "Bloggs",
66:     "email": "joe25@example.com"
67: }
68: ```
69: 
70: For a user with ID 4321 on the local database but no details have been set yet.
71: 
72: ```json
73: {
74:     "id": 4321,
75:     "first_name": "",
76:     "last_name": "",
77:     "email": ""
78: }
79: ```
80: 
81: ## Notes
82: 
83: * If the User does not have a `UserInfo` instance when requested then one will
84:   be created for them.
85: 404: Not Found404: Not Found404: Not Found404: Not Found

1: ---
2: stage: none
3: group: unassigned
4: info: For assistance with this Style Guide page, see <https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/product/ux/technical-writing/#assignments-to-other-projects-and-subjects>.
5: description: Writing styles, markup, formatting, and other standards for the GitLab RESTful APIs.
6: title: Documenting REST API resources
7: ---
8: 
9: REST API resources are documented in Markdown under
10: [`/doc/api`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/tree/master/doc/api). Each
11: resource has its own Markdown file, which is linked from
12: [`api_resources.md`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/doc/api/api_resources.md).
13: 
14: When modifying the Markdown or API code, also update the corresponding
15: [OpenAPI definition](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/tree/master/doc/api/openapi), by running
16: `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v2:generate` and `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v3:generate`.

305: ## cURL commands
306: 
307: - Use `https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/` as an endpoint.
308: - Wherever needed use this personal access token: `<your_access_token>`.
309: - Always put the request first. `GET` is the default so you don't have to
310:   include it.
311: - Use long option names (`--header` instead of `-H`) for legibility. (Tested in
312:   [`scripts/lint-doc.sh`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/scripts/lint-doc.sh).)
313: - Declare URLs with the `--url` parameter, and wrap the URL in double quotes (`"`).
314: - Prefer to use examples using the personal access token and don't pass data of
315:   username and password.
316: - For legibility, use the ` \ ` character and indentation to break long single-line
317:   commands apart into multiple lines.
318: 
319: | Methods                                         | Description                                            |
320: |-------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
321: | `--header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>"` | Use this method as is, whenever authentication needed. |
322: | `--request POST`                                | Use this method when creating new objects.             |

326: ## cURL Examples
327: 
328: The following sections include a set of [cURL](https://curl.se/) examples
329: you can use in the API documentation.
330: 
331: > [!warning]
332: > Do not use information for real users, URLs, or tokens. For documentation, refer to our
333: > relevant style guide sections on [fake user information](styleguide/_index.md#fake-user-information),
334: > [fake URLs](styleguide/_index.md#fake-urls), and [fake tokens](styleguide/_index.md#fake-tokens).
335: 
336: ### Simple cURL command
337: 
338: Get the details of a group:
339: 
340: ```shell
341: curl --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
342:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/groups/gitlab-org"
343: ```
344: 
345: ### cURL example with parameters passed in the URL
346: 
347: Create a new project under the authenticated user's namespace:
348: 
349: ```shell
350: curl --request POST --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
351:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects?name=foo"
352: ```
353: 
354: ### Post data using cURL's `--data`
355: 
356: Instead of using `--request POST` and appending the parameters to the URI, you
357: can use cURL's `--data` option. The example below creates a new project
358: `foo` under the authenticated user's namespace.
359: 
360: ```shell
361: curl --data "name=foo" \
362:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
363:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects"
364: ```
365: 
366: ### Post data using cURL's `--data-urlencode`
367: 
368: Use `--data-urlencode` when the data contains special characters that require URL encoding.
369: 
370: You can use this option for:
371: 
372: - Markdown content with code blocks or special formatting.
373: - Regular expressions containing `+`, `.`, or `*`.
374: - Text with quotes, ampersands, or other reserved URL characters.
375: - File content that might contain special characters.
376: 
377: For alphanumeric data without special characters, use [`--data`](#post-data-using-curls---data) instead.
378: 
379: For an attribute with special characters:
380: 
381: ```shell
382: curl --request POST \
383:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
384:   --data-urlencode "description=Fix issue with 'quotes' & ampersands" \
385:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/1/issues"
386: ```
387: 
388: For content with regular expression patterns:
389: 
390: ```shell
391: curl --request DELETE \
392:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
393:   --data-urlencode "name_regex_delete=dev-.+" \
394:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/5/registry/repositories/2/tags"
395: ```
396: 
397: For content from a file, use `attribute@filename`:
398: 
399: ```shell
400: curl --request POST \
401:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
402:   --data-urlencode "title=API documentation update" \
403:   --data-urlencode "content@content.md" \
404:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/1/wikis"
405: ```
406: 
407: ### Post data using JSON content
408: 
409: This example creates a new group. Be aware of the use of single (`'`) and double
410: (`"`) quotes.
411: 
412: ```shell
413: curl --request POST \
414:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
415:   --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
416:   --data '{"path": "my-group", "name": "My group"}' \
417:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/groups"
418: ```
419: 
420: For readability, you can also set up the `--data` by using the following format:
421: 
422: ```shell
423: curl --request POST \
424:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/groups" \
425:   --header "content-type: application/json" \
426:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
427:   --data '{
428:     "path": "my-group",
429:     "name": "My group"
430: }'
431: ```
432: 
433: ### Post data using form-data
434: 
435: Instead of using JSON or URL-encoding data, you can use `multipart/form-data` which
436: properly handles data encoding:
437: 
438: ```shell
439: curl --request POST \
440:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
441:   --form "title=ssh-key" \
442:   --form "key=ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EA..." \
443:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/users/25/keys"
444: ```
445: 
446: The above example adds an SSH public key titled `ssh-key` to the account of
447: a user with ID 25. The operation requires administrator access.
448: 
449: ### Escape special characters
450: 
451: Spaces or slashes (`/`) can sometimes result in errors, so you should
452: escape them when possible. In the example below we create a new issue which
453: contains spaces in its title. Observe how spaces are escaped using the `%20`
454: ASCII code.
455: 
456: ```shell
457: curl --request POST \
458:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
459:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/42/issues?title=Hello%20GitLab"
460: ```
461: 
462: Use `%2F` for slashes (`/`).
463: 
464: ### Pass arrays to API calls
465: 
466: The GitLab API sometimes accepts arrays of strings or integers. For example, to
467: exclude specific users when requesting a list of users for a project, you would
468: do something like this:
469: 
470: ```shell
471: curl --request PUT \
472:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>"
473:   --data "skip_users[]=<user_id>" \
474:   --data "skip_users[]=<user_id>" \
475:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/<project_id>/users"
476: ```
